attributes.Breed: Staffordshire Bull Terrier x Border Collie

name: Lucy
description:
Lucy came into our care through no fault of her own, along with her puppies. The puppies have all been rehomed now and after some patience, love and care Lucy is now ready to find her forever home. She is still very shy and scared if she doesn’t know you and will shout at you if you visit her in her kennel. Once she knows you, outside of the kennel, she is a very affectionate girl. She gets very excited to see you, so will jump all over you. She likes her treats which is a good way to help her build her confidence around new people. Lucy loves a run around in the compound area or walks in the woods. She is going to need an active family and plenty of mental stimulation to keep her occupied.

Lucy is looking for a very experienced home, with a family that have had nervous rescue dogs before. She is going to need a lot of patience and potential adopters are going to need to be able to commit to multiple meets before she goes home. Lucy is still just a young dog herself so will need all of the basic training and socialisation when she goes home. Lucy has the potential to be a lovely family dog but she does require time and work to help her reach this point.

Due to her being so nervous she needs to be in an adult only home with no visiting children.

Lucy has socialised well with dogs and loves a friend to go on walks with her. She can be very full on and over the top with dogs so would benefit from some further training to teach her some manners. We do believe that she can potentially be rehomed with another dog, it would have to be patient, gentle and of a similar size – subject to a successful meet.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Marlowe
description:
Marlowe is a super friendly bundle of Joy. Marlowe is still a young girl, so is looking for a family that has the time and energy to put in the work to help her grow to be a great companion. She is friendly with everyone she meets, staff and volunteers included. She can be very bouncy and does jump up to say hello. She can pull and get over excited on her lead when she goes out for walks. Marlowe’s favourite thing is running around off lead in our enclosed compound area, she is really interested in the agility equipment and loves jumping about on it. Marlowe would make a fantastic dog for someone who leads an active life and is looking for an energetic dog to take along with them. Due to her still being young she will need plenty of exercise and mental enrichment to keep her occupied, agility or scent work could be a good option for this. Marlowe as the potential to be a fantastic dog so just needs someone that is willing to put in the work and training that she requires.

Marlowe would be best suited to being with children who are 16 years and over, due to her coming in as a stray and having no background history on her – Subject to a successful meet.

Marlowe needs extra training around dogs as she is a little unsure on how to interact with them. Due to this she needs to be the only dog in the home.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Arlo
description:
Arlo is a gorgeous, sweet-natured boy who is very friendly and absolutely loves lots of fuss.  He’s a real people dog and enjoys getting plenty of attention and affection.  He is a very energetic and boisterous lad who can get extremely giddy when he’s excited.  He sometimes forgets just how big he is and will jump up to say hello, so he would benefit from some basic training to help him learn his manners and channel all that enthusiasm. Arlo loves running around in our compound area, getting out lots of energy with a case of the zoomies! Arlo is a loveable, fun, lively character with bags of personality.  He would thrive in a very active home with someone who can give him plenty of exercise, long walks and consistency with his training.  He would need a private secure garden so he can practice his zoomies!

Arlo has interacted well with dogs whilst in our care but can be very boisterous and jumpy, he could potentially be rehomed with a dog of a similar size and temperament – subject to a successful meet.

Arlo is best suited to be rehomed with children who are 16 years and over – subject to his successful meet.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Stevie
description:
Meet Stevie!  Stevie is our little nervous gentleman.  He is looking for a special home to call his own.  Stevie is a very timid and nervous little soul who has clearly found the world a little overwhelming.  Since coming into rescue, he has started to come around a little, but he still finds certain things difficult and needs an adopter who understands his worries and will respect his boundaries.  He can be a little growly if there are sudden movements around him or you approach him too fast, so it’s important that his new family understands this is his way of communicating that he feels uncomfortable or unsure.  He is now accepting the occasional gentle head stroke, but if we’re honest, Stevie isn’t particularly interested in lots of fuss or attention.  He’s quite happy having his own space and doing his own thing.  The quickest way to win Stevie over ?  A tasty treat! He is more than happy to come over when a tasty treat is on offer, although he’s very much there for the treat rather than a cuddle.  Stevie will need an experienced, calm and understanding home where there are no expectations placed upon him.  He needs people who are happy to let him settle at his own pace, give him plenty of space and allow him to decide when, and if, he wants interaction.  We aren’t looking for someone who wants a cuddly lap dog.  We are looking for someone who can appreciate a little old man for exactly who he is, without trying to change him.  Someone who understands that love sometimes means giving a dog the space to simply be.  Stevie is a nervous older gentleman who deserves a peaceful retirement, somewhere he can feel safe, secure and comfortable, with adopters who will respect his little quirks and never ask more of him than he can give.  He would benefit from a private secure garden.

Stevie has interacted with other dogs while in our care.  He can be a little barky and unsure with some and happy to have a sniff at others, so we feel he would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home where he doesn’t have to worry about another dog being around.  We want Stevie’s retirement to be as peaceful and stress-free as possible, so a pet-free home where he can have his own space and feel safe would be ideal for him.

As Stevie came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on him and as he is very nervous we would prefer any children/visiting children to be 16+ years.

name: Reggie
description:
Meet Reggie!  Reggie is a handsome young boy with a big personality and plenty of character!  Reggie is a friendly boy who enjoys interaction and playtime, but he is also a strong-minded lad who will need an experienced owner who understands his breed and can provide clear boundaries, consistency and guidance.  Reggie can become nippy when excited or overstimulated, so his new home will need to be mindful of his arousal levels and understand how to manage and redirect this behaviour appropriately.  He is also very vocal during play, so don’t be surprised if he has plenty to say!  He has some quirky behaviours too.  He loves chasing the hosepipe while staff are cleaning his kennel and can get quite enthusiastic and does rag his bedding.  His new adopter will need to show him how to channel that frustration.  Reggie can be quite dominant and has previously shown some possessive behaviour around his bed, standing over it while staff have attempted to move it.  He also displays some unusual body language at times, although he has been ok with staff during his time in our care.  We are looking for an experienced, confident and patient owner who can recognise and understand his body language, respect his boundaries and work positively with him to help him develop good manners and appropriate behaviours.  Reggie is still a young dog with lots to learn, and with the right home, consistent handling and ongoing training, we know he can continue to make progress.  He isn’t going to be the right match for everyone, but we believe the right person will see the lovely character behind this cheeky little Frenchie.  He will need a private secure garden.

Reggie has interacted with other dogs while in our care and is very humpy with them so we feel he would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home.

As Reggie came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Piglet
description:
Meet Piglet!  Piglet is a beautiful girl who is looking for a special home to call her own.  When Piglet first arrived with us, she was a very frightened little girl.  She would hide herself away in a corner, shaking and unsure of the world around her.  But with patience, reassurance and a few tasty treats, we’ve slowly started to see her lovely little personality shine through.  Piglet is the sweetest girl who absolutely loves affection once she feels safe.  She adores fuss and cuddles and will take any opportunity to jump up onto your lap for some attention.  She’s a real little love bug who just wants to feel safe and loved.  She is still a little unsure when out and about on a walk, so she’ll need someone willing to take things slowly and help build her confidence at her own pace.  Piglet is looking for a quiet, loving home where she can settle at her own pace, without too much pressure or expectation.  She will need understanding patient adopters who are happy to give her the time and reassurance she needs to feel secure.  Piglet may be a little nervous to begin with, but underneath that fear is a very sweet, affectionate girl who has so much love to give.   All she needs is someone to believe in her, give her time and show her the world can be a kind and safe place. She would benefit from a private secure garden.

Piglet has socialised well with other dogs while in our care, so we feel she could potentially live with another small calm dog following a successful meet and greet (must be neutered).

As Piglet came into us as a stray, we have no previous history on her and as she can be nervous we would prefer any children/visiting children to be 14+ years.

name: Lulu
description:
Meet Lulu!  When Lulu first arrived with us, she was a very nervous and timid girl who wasn’t quite sure of her surroundings.  However, with time, patience and kindness, she has really started to come out of her shell, and what a lovely little character she is.  Lulu is a very sweet girl who absolutely loves a fuss and enjoys attention from the people she knows and trusts.  She has made some lovely progress and is showing her little personality more everyday.  Now, we should mention that Lulu does have a cheeky side!  She’s quite the escape artist and will often try to sneak past staff when they enter her kennel.  She’s certainly a girl who likes to keep us on our toes, so her new adopter will need to be mindful of open doors and make sure the can’t make a great escape!  Lulu also has a sensitive tummy, so she is currently fed on sensitive dog food to help keep this settled.  As Lulu was initially quite nervous, she may need a little time to settle and build her confidence in a new home.  She will need a patient, understanding family who are happy to let her take things at her own pace, giving her the love and reassurance she needs to feel safe and secure.  This sweet girl deserves a loving forever home where she can continue to blossom and show just how wonderful she really is.  She will need a private secure garden.

Lulu has socialised well with other dogs while in our care, so we feel she could potentially be rehomed with another dog following a successful meet and greet (must be neutered).

As Lulu came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on her, so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Fizz
description:
Meet Fizz!  Fizz is a beautiful girl with a big personality and bags of character.  She is a friendly, excitable and very playful little lady who is always ready to bring a bit of fun and mischief wherever she goes.  She’s a sassy girl who knows her own mind and certainly isn’t short of personality.  Fizz absolutely loves human company and thrives on attention.  She’s a girl who enjoys being involved in everything and will jump up to say hello and demand some fuss.  She would benefit from continued gentle guidance with her manners and to be shown there are calmer ways to say hello.  When she gets a little overexcited, she does gently nibble at your fingers, but this is all part of her excited and playful nature and is done without any malice.  She’s a giddy, fun-loving girl who loves her walks and enjoys getting out and about to explore.  Whether it’s playtime, walkies or simply spending time with her favourite people. Fizz is happiest when she’s getting attention and being part of the action.  Fizz is looking for a home that will embrace her cheeky character, enjoy her playful ways and give her all the love, time and attention she deserves.  She will need continued guidance on how to manager her excitement.  She would benefit from a private secure garden.

Fizz has interacted with other dogs while in our care, and although she is happy to walk along side them she doesn’t like them in her face or sniffing around her back end so we feel she would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home.

As Fizz came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Darren
description:
Darren came into our care as a stray so we don’t have any background information about him. He is looking for a very special home with someone who truly understands the unique personality and characteristics of the Shar – Pei Breed. Like many Shar -Pei’s, he is an independent character who enjoys doing things on his own terms. He isn’t fussed about being handled, fussed over or touched and prefers his own personal space respected. He needs an understanding owner who can recognise his body language, respect his boundaries and give him time to build trust at his own pace. Whilst he may not be a cuddly, affectionate dog, he has his own personality and charm.

He really enjoys getting out on walks and it’s great to see him perk up with excitement as soon as he spots the lead, it certainly is the highlight of his day! He is strong on the lead and does pull a lot so he will need more work in this area. He has socialised well with dogs out on walks and has shown that he can be comfortable out in  a group.

Darren needs an experienced adult only home, with no visiting children.

Darren is best suited to being the only dog in the home so he can have his own space.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Theo
description:
Meet Theo! Theo has a big heart and plenty of love to give.  This friendly, affectionate boy absolutely thrives on attention, and the more fuss and cuddles he gets, the happier he is!  Theo loves getting out and about on walks (he does walk better on a harness) but his favourite time of days is his off-lead time in our secure compound where he can run around and chase his favourite toys.  He does know some basic commands like sit, paw and speak and is very eager to please.  Theo can bark to get your attention and tends to jump up when he gets excited.  He will benefit from a family who can continue working with him on his manners and help him learn calmer ways to ask for attention.  Theo is a fun-loving affectionate boy who has so much love to give.  He would love a home where he can enjoy his walks, have plenty of playtime and, most importantly, receive all the love and attention he deserves.  Theo will need a private secure garden so he can safely have off-lead time with his toys.

Theo has socialised with other dogs while in our care, he will have a quick sniff but isn’t too bothered about them, so we feel he would be happiest being the only dog in the home where he can receive 100% of the attention and cuddles.

Theo has a Grade 1 Heart Murmur, this will be discussed in more detail with the successful applicant.

As Theo came into us as a stray we have no previous history on him, so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Frank
description:
Frank is a sweet-natured boy who absolutely loves people and enjoys being the centre of attention.  He is a very giddy and excitable character, and his enthusiasm can sometimes get the better of him!  Frank loves treats and is always keen to show off what he knows.  He has his basic commands and is eager to learn, especially when there’s a tasty reward involved.  He can be quite vocal in his kennel, and when excited he can become a little mouthy.  He also loves attention and will jump up to say hello, so his new adopter will need to be comfortable helping him learn some calmer ways to greet people.

Frank is a strong boy on the lead and will need continued training and guidance with his lead manners.  He is an active dog who needs plenty of exercise as well as mental stimulation to keep his busy mind occupied.  Frank is looking for an active and committed home where his new family can give him the exercise, enrichment, training and attention he needs.  His ideal home will be one where his adopters understand that he is an excitable, energetic boy and are prepared to work with him on his manners and impulse control.  In return, Frank has so much affection and enthusiasm to give.  He will need a private secure garden.

We think that Frank can be rehomed with dog savvy children who are 16 years and over due to his size and strength – subject to a successful meet.

Frank has interacted well with dogs whilst in our care so we feel that he could potentially be rehomed with another dog of a similar size and temperament – subject to a successful meet.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Jax
description:
Jax is a friendly and affectionate boy who absolutely loves attention and enjoys a good fuss.  He has a wonderful nature and is always happy to spend time with his people. This clever lad is exceptionally well behaved at the vets, taking examinations and handling in his stride, which is a testament to his temperament and trainability.  Like many dogs, he has his own little quirks – one of his favourites is enthusiastically ragging his blankets and rearranging them to his liking!

As a typical Belgian Malinois, he is highly intelligent, energetic and thrives on both physical exercise and mental stimulation.  He loves charging around our compound and would be happiest in a home where he has plenty of opportunities to stay active and engaged.  Jax is very ball focused which is a bonus when it comes to training. Because of his breed traits, he will need an owner who has previous experience with Belgian Malinois and understands their needs.  He is not a dog that will be content with a short walk around the block, he requires ongoing training, enrichment and a lifestyle that allows him to use both his body and brain.  He will need a private secure garden.

We feel that it would be best for Jax to be rehomed with adults only.

Jax is a typical Mali so likes to be vocal around other dogs, he is easily distracted with toys but we feel like he would be best suited to being the only dog in the home so he can have his own space and the focus on him.

No cats or small furries for Jax due to having a very high prey drive. We would recommend not having any cats within your area.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Rudy
description:
Don’t let his age fool you, this lively, energetic boy has plenty of energy and enthusiasm. Rudy is a friendly, excitable and affectionate boy who absolutely loves attention and fuss.  He has a big personality and is not shy about letting you know when he wants you to interact with him!  Rudy can be quite vocal when he wants your attention or, more importantly, when he thinks it’s time for you to throw his ball.  Rudy’s favourite thing to do is chase his toys, and he could happily spend all afternoon playing and having fun.  He also enjoys his long walks and would love an active home who can provide him with plenty of exercise and opportunities to explore.

Rudy is a strong boy on the lead, so his new adopters will need to be confident handling him and willing to continue working on his lead manners.  He does know his basic commands and with the right guidance, could continue to build on these. He would suit someone who enjoys getting out and about and is looking for a fun, lively companion with a larger-than-life  personality.

We think that Rudy could be rehomed with children who are 13 years and over – subject to a successful meet.

Rudy has interacted well with dogs whilst in our care so we believe that he could potentially be rehomed with another dog of similar size and temperament – subject to a successful meet.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Pearl
description:
Pearl came into our care as a stray so we don’t have much of a history on her. She can be a little vocal around people at first but soon warms up with treats. She is a very sweet gentle girl when she knows you and loves a good fuss. Pearl is an old girl so is looking for a calm, quiet loving home to spend the rest of her years. Pearl loves to curl up under a blanket to keep warm after a nice walk with lots of sniffing. She is still eager to go for a walk and does also enjoy a good run around our enclosed compound area when she has the chance. She loves a boomer ball! Pearl is very food motivated which is a bonus for getting to know her. Pearl would be best suited to a home that has owned a Frenchie before. Due to her older age she does have a few health issues that can be discussed further if you are successful.

We think that Pearl would be best suited to an adult only home.

Pearl has interacted well with dogs whilst in our care, so she can potentially be rehomed with another dog- subject to a successful meet. This dog will need to be of a similar size and a calm  temperament.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Mavis
description:
Mavis came into our care as a stray so we don’t have any history on her. She is a typical Frenchie that likes her own way, especially around new people. She is quite protective of her kennel so will shout at you if you come near her. Out on a walk she is much more confident and can be handled. She is just a cheeky girl! She does like attention and a fuss, on her terms, once she gets to know you. She has the potential to be a very loving companion, she just needs the right home that has the patience to allow her to settle down into a new environment. She may need some basic training once she gets home as we are not sure if she has lived in a home before. Mavis needs an experienced home, either with the breed or with nervous rescue dogs.

Mavis needs to be in an adult only home, no visiting children.

Mavis has socialised well with dogs whilst in our care but we believe she would be best suited to being the only dog in the home.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Dean
description:
Dean is a very friendly boy, he likes to say hello to everyone he meets and loves a fuss. He was a little nervous when he first came in though, it has taken some time for him to reach this point. He loves his toys and can play independently with them in his kennel, he has a favourite toy here which is a string of sausages! He’s a big foody and loves all kinds of tasty snacks. He also enjoys his walks around the woods taking in all of the different smells. With him being a stray there is a possibility that he’s never lived in a home before so some training might be needed to help settle him in. Experience with Frenchie’s is preferred, as they usually have cheeky personalities once they have settled.

Dean needs to be the only dog in the home. He needs continuous socialisation training around dogs to help build his confidence as he can be a little snappy and unsure of new dogs. He has little dog syndrome! His new family must be committed to taking him to training classes.

Dean is best suited to be rehomed with children who are 16 years and over – subject to a successful meet.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Ronnie
description:
Ronnie was very nervous and shut down when he first arrived, very unsure of everyone and didn’t know who he could trust. With time and patients from staff, Ronnie is now a completely different dog. He is a super happy boy, who absolutely loves everyone he meets. As soon as he sees you he’s instantly wiggly and gets all giddy. Ronnie brings a smile to everyone’s face with his amazing personality.

With Ronnie having lots of energy and being super playful, he is looking for an active home. His new home must be an adult only home, due to how nervous he was initial here at the home.

We don’t believe Ronnie would be suitable to live with cats or small animals.

Whilst in our care, Ronnie has socialised really well with other dogs. Therefore, we believe he could potentially live with another dog of a similar temperament and able to deal with his craziness – subject to a successful meet.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Wayne
description:
Wayne will do anything for a good cuddle, he is a super affectionate boy who loves all the attention. He is very giddy and gets very excited when he sees you and even more excited when it’s time for his walk. Wayne can jump up with excitement, so would benefit from further training with this. As he is still a young boy, he is looking for an active home able to give him the exercise he requires.

Since being in our care, Wayne has socialised well with other dogs and enjoys their company whilst out on walks. Therefore, we do believe he could potentially live with another dog of a similar temperament and able to keep up with his craziness – subject to a successful meet.

We don’t have any previous history on Wayne as he sadly came into our care as a stray. We believe he could potentially live with children no younger than 14 years old – subject to a successful meet.

Wayne wouldn’t be suitable to live with cats or small animals.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Merida
description:
Merida came into our care as stray, therefore we don’t have any previous history on her. When she first arrived at the home, Merida was very nervous and a shy girl. She slowly started to trust staff but can still be nervous and unsure when meeting new people, especially men. Merida is looking for a very patient home, who are understanding and must be committed to do multiple meets here at the home.

Once out of her shell and is confident with you, she’s an absolute sweetheart. Full of life and energy. She thoroughly enjoys being outside on her daily walks. Merida is also super playful, always enjoying time in our enclosed area, playing with toys and staff. Her new family must be active and happy to take her on new adventures.

Whilst being in our care, Merida prefers her own space with other dogs and doesn’t like to be bothered by them. For this reason, she would be best suited to a home with no other dogs. Her new family must be willing to continue with her socialising.

Due to her nervousness, Merida is needing an adult only home, with no visiting children either. She needs a quieter home where she can settle at her pace and feel comfortable. Her new home must be experience and ideally dealt with nervous dogs before.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Rambo
description:
Meet Rambo!  He is a gorgeous boy with a heart full of love.  Rambo is a very sweet affectionate lad who loves spending time outside and enjoying the world around him.  He has so much to offer the right family and is looking for a home where he can truly thrive.  Kennel life is incredibly stressful for Rambo.  He struggles with being confined, often scratching and climbing the bars when he becomes overwhelmed.  However, once he is out of his kennel, he relaxes enjoys his surroundings and is a very happy boy with his tail wagging like mad.  Being returned to his kennel is particularly difficult for him, so he would benefit hugely from a home where he can feel safe, settled and secure.  Rambo loves  – long walks getting out and about, off-lead time in our secure compound where he can chase around with his toys, being brushed and enjoying a little pampering and spending time with people receiving lots of fuss and strokes.  Rambo walks nicely on the lead, making him  a lovely companion for someone who enjoys getting outdoors.  As a Husky, he would need an active lifestyle filled with long walks, hikes, adventures and plenty of opportunities to explore.  Rambo is looking for an active, loving home that understands his needs and can offer him time, exercise and the companionship he deserves.  He will need a private secure garden where he can safely enjoy some off lead time as well as an adopter that is committed to keeping him mentally and physically stimulated.  Most importantly, Rambo needs a home where he can feel relaxed and comfortable, away from the stress of kennel life.

Rambo has socialised well with other dogs while in our care, so we feel he could potentially be rehomed with another dog of similar size following a successful meet and greet.

As Rambo came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

If you have a holiday in the next 3 months, please wait until you reply to apply for a dog.

name: Tommy
description:
Tommy is an ex racing greyhound who has spent his life in kennels. He is now looking for a comfortable and loving home to call his own. He will need a family that is happy to introduce and train him around everything that is involved in living in a home environment. Tommy is a very affectionate boy and has been described as a velcro dog by the kennel staff. He is after a home where he can get plenty of attention and cuddles throughout the day. He is a big foodie and is motivated by treats, which is a bonus to help with training.

Tommy is confident around staff and volunteers but due to his size we believe that he would be best suited to an adult only home.

Tommy is a little unsure around most dogs so will need further positive training to help build up his confidence in this area. He is currently paired with another greyhound in the kennel and has has no issues with her, so we believe that he could be rehomed with another calm greyhound or sighthound – subject to a successful meet.

No cats or small furries for Tommy due to his racing background.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Derby
description:
Derby is a sensitive, gentle soul who is still finding his feet and learning that the world doesn’t have to be a scary place. A lot of things at the moment are frightening for him, but we are beginning to see small glimpses of his confidence growing. Although he can be very nervous, underneath his worries is an incredibly affectionate boy who absolutely loves human company. He really enjoys cuddles and gentle strokes, if you dare to stop fussing him, he will reach out with his paw and ask for more. It is impossible not to fall in love with his sweet personality. He spends much of his time curled up on his comfy bed, where he feels safe and secure, but he will pop out to say hello when a familiar face visits his kennel. He enjoys a run around to stretch his legs in compound area, but isn’t sure about toys yet so would much rather stay close his his handler.

He’s had positive, friendly interactions with other dogs so we believe that he could potentially be re homed with a dog of a calm temperament and similar size – subject to a successful meet.

Due to his nervous nature we believe that Derby would be best suited to living in a calm house with children who are 16 years and over – subject to success meet. It is likely that he would need multiple meets to get to know his new family before he goes home.

If you feel that you could provide Derby with a peaceful, patient and understanding forever home please apply for Derby today!

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Amanda
description:
Amanda came into our care as a stray so we don’t have any background information on her. She was a little unsure and nervous when she first arrived but has slowly started to come out of her shell. She can be affectionate once she knows you. She is a typical cheeky Frenchie who likes to have her own way. She is looking for a home with a family that has previous experience or knowledge of the breed and is happy to work with her until she is more settled. We believe that Amanda may need some basic training to help her improve her manners in the home.

Amanda has socialised well with dogs whilst in our care but we feel that she would be best suited to the only dog in the home.

We feel that Amanda would be best suited for an adult only home, no visiting children.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Chopper
description:
Meet Chopper! (27kg) Chopper is a very sweet and friendly boy who has so much love to give. When he first came into our care, he was very barky, but as soon as he got to know the staff and felt safe his personality began to shine through.  He loves a fuss and attention and is always happy to come over for some affection.  He does sometimes forget quite how strong he is when he comes over to say hello – he can be a little enthusiastic with his greetings.  But underneath his big personality is a lovely, affectionate boy who enjoys spending time with people.  Chopper can be quite vocal while in his kennel, but once he is out and about he settles nicely.  He particularly enjoys his off-lead time in our secure compound where he can have a good run.  He also loves getting out for walks in the area exploring, he can be strong on the lead so will need continued lead training.  He would benefit from an active family that can continue giving him plenty of exercise and enrichment.  Chopper will need someone who is willing to commit to his training and socialisation.  Sadly, Chopper came into our care with cropped ears.  His ears will need to be regularly monitored and cared for to ensure they remain healthy, and this will need to be considered by anyone looking to offer him a home.  We are looking for a committed home who will give Chopper the time, structure, exercise and affection he deserves.  In return, you’ll have a loving, fun and affectionate boy who is ready to enjoy the next chapter of his life.  He will need a private secure garden.

Chopper has interacted ok with other dogs whilst in our care, but we do feel he would be best rehomed as the only dog in the household where he can get 100% of the attention and training.

As Chopper came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Rafi
description:
Rafi is a lively, happy boy with a cheeky personality. Rafi is still just a young boy who is in need of a stable and loving home. He is after a family that is happy to put in a lot of time and effort into his training to help him improve his manners. Dobermans are a breed that need to be worked with for their entire life so we are after someone who is fully committed to taking on this responsibility. Experience with this breed or similar is also a must.

Rafi is going to need a large fully enclosed garden that he can have off lead time in, to burn off energy and to help with his training. Rafi will need plenty of walks and mental stimulation to keep him occupied so he doesn’t cause too much mischief. Rafi would benefit from a home where someone is around a lot and has plenty of free time to focus on him and his training.

Rafi is best suited to an adult only home, with no visiting children.

Rafi needs to be the only dog in the home, no visiting dogs either. Rafi is currently under going socialisation training with dogs to help improve his reactivity. This is something that will need to be continued when he goes home and into the future.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Todd
description:
This handsome boy is Todd!  Todd is a sweet, friendly and very lively boy with plenty of energy to spare!  He is a typical hound in many ways – full of enthusiasm, curious about the world around him and always ready for his next adventure.  He absolutely loves his off-lead time in our secure compound where he can stretch his legs, explore, have a sniff and have fun with his favourite toys.  Watching Todd enjoy himself is a real pleasure! As you would expect from a Fox Hound, Todd is high-energy and needs a very active home that can provide him with plenty of daily exercise.  Walks alone may not be enough to keep his body and mind satisfied, so he would really benefit from additional activities such as scent work, tracking games, enrichment and other opportunities to use his wonderful Hound brain.  Todd is also a vocal boy – hounds are known for their voices, and Todd is certainly not shy about using his!  His new family will need to appreciate that hound singing, baying and general commentary are part of the package.  Hounds are also known for being escape artists so he will need secure, hound-proof fencing and careful management, particularly when he is outdoors. A home that understands the determination and curiosity of a scent-driven hound would be ideal.  Todd has so much character and has all the makings of a fantastic companion in the right home.  He needs someone who understands that a Fox Hound is a lifestyle, not just a pet – but for the right home, Todd will bring plenty of fun, affection and adventure.

Todd has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care and is very playful and full-on.  We do feel he could potentially live with another dog of similar energy levels that would tolerate his play style following a successful meet and greet.

As Todd came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Shadow
description:
Shadow is a very affectionate boy who has been super friendly to our staff and volunteers since he came in to our care. With him being an ex racer, he does have a high prey drive so can try to chase squirrels whilst out for his walks! He absolutely loves chasing his toys around our secure compound.  He is a really affectionate boy who loves lots of fuss and attention.

Shadow will have spent most of his life in kennels with his racing background, so he may feel a little nervous going in to a home environment. We also do not know if he is house trained or toilet trained due to this. He loves to lie in his comfy beds after his walks – we sometimes catch him upside down showing his belly off!

Shadow has now been in our care for 237 days and is desperately searching for his forever home.

We think Shadow would prefer to be the only dog in the home as he can sometimes be a little unsure around them and isn’t too interested in interacting with them.

He could also potentially live with children 14+ years  – subject to a successful meet.

Shadow would love a home where he could relax and enjoy his retirement years and rest on a comfy bed (or couch) of his own!

name: Prince
description:
Prince came into our care as a stray so we don’t have much history on him. We do believe that he could have potentially lived in a home previously and that he isn’t from a racing background. Prince is a happy excitable boy that jumps up in the kennel when you go into him. He can get very giddy for his walks and loves to be outside taking in all of the different smells. Prince has enjoyed different kinds of enrichment in between his walks and loves playing with his toys. He is a sweet boy who is after a loving forever home.

Prince has been rehomed recently but showed signs of  having separation anxiety so he is in need of a home where someone is around most of the time and is able to build up his time being left. Experience with sight hounds or rescue dogs will be beneficial to ensure that he is getting the training that he needs to settle into a new home.

Prince would be best suited to a home with children who are 16 years and over due to his bouncy nature – subject to a successful meet.

Prince initially could be vocal around dogs due to being a little unsure, we have now found out this is due to him wanting to say hello. He has been on group walks recently and loved interacting with other dogs and saying hello. He can be very enthusiastic when meeting dogs so we need someone that is able to physically hold onto him so he can continue on with his socialisation  training and learn better manners around dogs. We still think it would be best for him to be the only dog in the home so he can be the main focus.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Swan
description:
Swan came into our care as a stray, meaning we don’t have any previous history on her. She is a very friendly and affection girl, who loves nothing more than a good cuddle with you. As Swan is still young, she would be best suited to an active home able to give her the regular exercise that she requires. Swan thoroughly enjoys playing in our enclosed area where she loves playing and chasing tennis balls.

At times Swan can be a little boisterous and fully on when she gets all excited to see you. We believe she would be best suited to a home with children no younger than 16 years old – subject to a successful meet.

During her time with us, Swan has shown to a social towards other dogs, although at times can be a little over the top and vocal, which is typical of her breed. We do think she would prefer to be only dog in the home, where she can happily play with her own toys and not share her space.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Hero
description:
Hero is an ex racing greyhound who is now looking for his forever home with a family that can help him settle into life beyond the kennels. He is a confident, lively boy with plenty of personality. He gets very excited when it’s time for a walk and can jump around on the lead, so will need someone who is comfortable handling a tall strong greyhound. With a little training and consistency this is something that can be worked on. Although he is confident in many ways, he does need help building his confidence when it comes to being touched and handled as he can get a little worried.  Hero deserves the chance to learn, grow and discover just how good life can be outside of kennels.

Hero can be rehomed with mature children who are 16 years and over, due to his size and bouncy nature. This will be subject to a successful meet.

Hero is currently paired with another greyhound and has interreacted well with dogs whilst in our care, so we believe that he would be rehomed with another dog- subject to a successful meet and greet.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Bear
description:
Bear is a very nervous boy when he meets new people for the first time. It takes a little while for him to come around but with patience and yummy treats he slowly starts to trust you. Once he has gained your trust and is comfortable he is an affectionate boy and loves to give out kisses. He will need to have multiple regular meets before going home.

Bear is a big dog who doesn’t understand his size, he is constantly jumping up for cuddles and doesn’t know what personal space is. Bear is going to require a lot of training to help him learn manners. He can be a very cheeky boy at times! He will need socialising in different environments and around people to help him build his confidence up. Bear gets super excited when going for walks and is very strong on the lead, this is another area that will need more training. Bear loves playing with his toys, splashing around in water and zooming around our enclosed area.

Bear is after an adult only home that has previous experience with big boisterous dogs. No regular visiting children either please. He is going to need a very active home with a family that is able to provide him with plenty of exercise and mental stimulation to keep him busy. As he is still only a young dog he can get up to mischief when he is bored. Bear’s new family need to be committed to putting in the training that he needs not only initially but keeping it up for the rest of his life.

Bear needs to be the only dog in the home so that he can have all of attention to help get him settled. Bear can interact well with dogs whilst out on walks but will need further training to help improve this.

We know that Bear is going to require a lot of work at first but once he is trained he will make a lovely family dog who will love going on plenty of adventures. Taking on a dog this size is a big commitment, please ensure that you are serious and have thought about the future before applying.

name: Ripley
description:
Meet Ripley!! He is a gorgeous boy looking for an active, committed home where he can continue to learn and thrive.  He’s a friendly, affectionate boy with a fun-loving personality and is always ready for a game with his favourite toys.  He is full of energy and loves to play, so he will need an active family who can provide plenty of exercise, enrichment, and ongoing training.  Like many young dogs, he can become a little mouthy and nippy when he’s excited, so he will benefit from patient guidance and positive reinforcement to help him learn appropriate manners.  He is still working on his basic commands and will need someone willing to continue his training.  He can also occasionally rag his lead, so further lead training will be important.  Previous experience with Shar-pei’s would be a real advantage, as they can have their own unique characteristics and training needs.  He currently has a cherry eye, which will be surgically repaired before he goes to his new home, so he’ll be ready to start his next chapter feeling his best.  If you’re looking for a playful, lively young dog and have to time and commitment to help him become the wonderful companion we know he can be, Ripley could be the boy for you.

Ripley has socialised well with other dogs and is very playful with them.  He can sometimes get frustrated and bark if he can’t get to them straight away.  We feel he could potentially be rehomed with another playful dog of similar size following a successful meet and greet.

As Ripley came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him and as he can be a little nippy when over-excited we would like any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Star
description:
Star is a typical Patterdale Terrier who is always raring to go! She loves being outdoors, exploring new smells and trying to chase any wildlife she comes across. Star would love a fully enclosed garden where she can enjoy plenty of secure off-lead time and burn off some of her energy. Patterdale experience is essential as she can have her cheeky moments and will need a family who understands her spirited nature. Star has been rehomed twice previously so is looking for a patient family that has a lot of experience with dogs that need extra training and time to settle into a new life in a home.

We have found that Star struggles when left alone, so her new family will need to be around for most of the time. She will need someone who has the time, patience and commitment to help her settle into her new life and feel comfortable in a home environment. As Star was found as a stray, we don’t have much background information about her. However, we know she is an energetic, characterful girl who will thrive with the right family, plenty of exercise and lots of love.

Star may require multiple meets so she can get to know her new family before going home. Her new family will need to be patient and understanding whilst she is settling in and getting used to her new surroundings.

We think that it is best for Star to be rehomed to an adult only home with no visiting children.

Star can be very vocal around dogs and get overwhelmed easily so will need to be the only dog in the home. She will need continuous training to help her improve her confidence.

We wouldn’t recommend Star to be rehomed with cats due to her breed.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Nibbles
description:
Nibbles is a young boy who is full of energy and has a lot of love to give. Nibbles loves being off lead in our enclosed area running around chasing tennis balls. He has a lot of energy so will need a very active home with a family who can take him out on lots of adventures to burn off his energy. He would benefit from mental stimulation in between walks to keep his brain stimulated. Due to being a young dog Nibbles will need further training to help him grow up to be a well mannered boy, he can be a little nippy at times too.

Nibbles came into our care as a stray so we don’t have any history on him. Due to being very friendly we think that he can be rehomed with dog savvy children who are 16 years and older – subject to a successful meet.

Nibbles is friendly with every dog he meets and always wants to play. He can potentially be rehomed with another dog that can tolerate his high energy and playfulness – subject to a successful meet.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Elias
description:
Elias is a very sweet and friendly boy. He came into our care as a stray so we don’t have any background information on him. He has always been friendly with staff and volunteers whilst here. Elias can be a little strong on the lead due to his size so some basic lead training would be beneficial for him. We are looking for an active home for Elias as he has a lot of energy and would enjoy going on lots of adventures. Elias is a calm boy in his kennel and loves to have some down time with a tasty chew.

Elias is a friendly boy but due to his size we believe that it would be best for him to be rehomed with children over 14 years and over – Subject to a successful meet.

Elias needs a little more training around dogs since his castration as he has become a little unsure, therefore we believe that Elias would benefit from being the only dog in the home as he would prefer all the attention on him.

name: Ronnie
description:
Ronnie is a cheeky girl who is looking for a caring forever home. She is a bouncy girl that is full of energy and would love to go out for lots of adventures. She constantly wants to be out on walks and tries her hardest to escape from the kennel when the door is open- she’s a cheeky monkey! She is super friendly with everyone she meets and enjoys shouting at you if you try to ignore her- she constantly wants attention. Ronnie has shown signs of separation anxiety so is looking for an experienced home that has dealt with this previously. Ronnie is a typical Frenchie so she is in need of a home that has owned Frenchie’s previously.

She is a friendly girl but can get a little jealous when the attention isn’t on her, so we believe it would be best for her to be in an adult only home with no visiting children. Ronnie would be best suited to a quiet home with not many visitors.

Ronnie has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care, however, we believe she would be best suited to a home where she can be the only dog, so she can have all the attention and love. She may need on going socialisation training around dogs due to her being in the kennels for so long.

name: Sam
description:
Sam is a very loveable boy who just wants to give out hugs to everyone he meets, he does sometimes forget how big he is though. He’s a big hit with volunteers here and they all love taking him out for his walks as they get to have lots of cuddles. He can be strong on the lead though due to his size. He’s a very sweet boy who has a big heart and is looking for someone to show him lots of love! Sam has enjoyed his walks around the woods, watching the ducks and wildlife around him. Sam would appreciate an enclosed garden that he can spend his time in relaxing and enjoying the sun. Sam loves his treats, nothing is too big or small for him – he isn’t fussy!

Sam is super friendly with everyone he meets but due to his giddy jumpy nature we believe that it would be best to rehome Sam with children over the age of 16 – subject to a successful meet and greet.

Sam needs to be the only dog in the home, he can be vocal around dogs so needs a family that has experience to help build his confidence and manners.

If you think that you could provide a comfortable home with lots of treats for Sam please apply now!

name: Florence
description:
Florence is super friendly and loves everyone that she meets! She likes to leave her mark on you in the form of drool! She absolutely loves her food and isn’t fussy at all – she will eat anything. She has recently been on a diet and her new home must be willing to continue this to help her reach her ideal weight. When you go to see her in the kennel, she is so wriggly and happy and just wants love and affection all the time. She will jump up at you to give kisses and doesn’t realise what a big chunk she is! Florence needs a home that can provide her with short walks throughout the day to help with her weight loss. Florence needs a fully enclosed private garden that she can use in between her walks, she wouldn’t be suitable to live in a flat.

Florence is looking for a adult only home. She would prefer a home where someone is around for most of the day so she can have lots of cuddles.

Florence can be a little unsure around other dogs. We have been working on socialisation with her to get her used to other dogs but this is something her new family will need to keep up so she can build her confidence. Due to this, she would be most comfortable being the only dog in the home.

name: Rebecca
description:
I can live with older dog-savvy children who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I'm new to lead walking and need some practice!

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before

I've started my vaccinations and will be spayed before adoption.

22-10-26 Rebecca is a very sweet but scared girl who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is quite shy, but we can approach her slowly and put a lead on her. Rebecca is a little hand-shy, although she will accept gentle fuss and handling. She is still unsure of us and will need time to feel comfortable, but we hope that with patience and kindness, she will gradually come out of her shell. However, the more she gets to know you, she feels more comfortable with you and will come up to you for a gentle fuss.

We believe that Rebecca will need another kind and confident dog in her new home, as this dog will be a much-needed support system for her. Having a reassuring canine companion by her side should help her feel more secure as she settles in and gets used to her new surroundings. She will need a home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeders, and can live with older-dog savvy children who are sensible and allow her time to settle in.

As Rebecca has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. She has taken to lead walking quite well, so once she is settled in, we think she would enjoy one or two walks around the local area with her resident dog.

Rebecca is a sweet girl who is still finding her confidence, and we hope that with the support of a kind canine companion and a patient family, she will slowly begin to feel more comfortable and enjoy all the happiness and comforts that a loving home can bring.

Rebecca has been given the Gift of Life by Carol Keating

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Otis
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden with 6ft+ fences.

I have started harness training, but this is still new to me!

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home!

Otis has come to us from a breeder to find his forever home. He is an extremely nervous boy who is still finding the world a very scary place and is utterly petrified of human touch. When he first arrived, he would do everything he could to avoid being touched, frantically running around the yard to escape contact. Although he was interested in people, he simply didn't feel brave enough to let them close.

Otis is now making small but lovely steps forward, although he is still extremely worried about touch, with those who he knows very well he will tentatively accept chin tickles, though is still very worried about this. He still needs to build his confidence, and getting him comfortable with human hands will be a slow process that is likely to continue well into his new home. His adopters must be prepared to work at his pace, without rushing or putting pressure on him.

At just one year old, Otis has plenty of typical Labrador puppy character waiting to shine through. He loves tennis balls and soft toys and is still figuring out how to play fetch! As his confidence grows, we're beginning to see more of his funny, silly personality, and we hope there is lots more to come.

Otis absolutely adores other dogs and takes great comfort and reassurance from their company. He will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in his new home to help him feel safe and guide him as he learns about life in a home. Having a canine friend by his side will be particularly important while he continues to build trust in people.

Otis will need a calm, quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and understand the time and patience they need. He has never lived in a home before, so he will need help learning all about home life, including house training. He will also need a secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft to keep him safe while he gains confidence.

Otis has started harness training with his kennel mummy, and this will need to continue in his home at a slow and comfortable pace. This will need to be introduced gradually, starting in a safe environment and allowing him to progress at his own pace.

Otis is a special little boy who is trying so hard to be brave. With patient, understanding adopters and a confident canine companion, we believe he has the potential to blossom into a fun, loving and rewarding companion. He will need a family willing to celebrate the smallest steps forward and give him the time he needs to discover that the world can be a wonderful place.

Otis has been given the Gift of Life by Nic Johhston

Otis is a few weeks into his stay at Many Tears and honestly, he’s breaking my heart. That being said, he is progressing slowly, in his own funny way.

Otis is utterly petrified of human touch and when he first arrive he would do literally anything to get away from me. I mean truly frantic to avoid being touched. He would bolt away in the yard and do laps to avoid any contact. He wouldn’t take treats from my hand despite being a massive foodie! Yet when I turned around he would show interest to me and would nibble my hand through the gates. He so wanted to be brave and just didn’t know how.

We are slowly getting there, it’s not much of a progression to most people but he will freeze with me now and tentatively accept chin tickles. Small baby steps, we are already seeing progress! Desensitising Otis to human hands is not going to be a quick fix and will likely continue into his home life. He does now take treats from my hand, even in the yard but after each treat he does a little lap of the yard to ramp himself up for the next one! He really is such a funny little guy.

At just 1 years old, he has so much of your typical Lab puppy in him, but he just doesn’t feel safe enough to fully let it out. He loves a tennis ball and is still coming to grips with how fetch works. He loves soft toys and ADORES the company of other dogs and seeks so much comfort and support from them.

Once Otis is more comfortable being handled, our next milestone will be getting him in a harness to begin the road to exploring the world on walks!

He is such a character & the more confident he becomes, the more we get to see his funny, silly side. I really do believe he will settle into the most fulfilling, fun dog you could hope for & will make his future adopters very happy!

Otis has come to us from a breeder to find his forever home. He is a very nervous boy who is feeling very overwhelmed by all the changes in his life and is finding his surroundings quite scary at the moment. He is very worried about being handled and it is clear that he has not had much socialisation before, so he is in need of lots of patience, kindness and TLC.

Otis will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have experience with scared ex-breeding dogs and understand that he will need plenty of time to settle in and build his confidence at his own pace. He will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in his new home to be his friend and companion and help show him the ropes. Having a confident canine friend by his side will be very important as Otis begins to learn that the world is not such a scary place.

Otis will also need a secure garden with 6ft+ fencing to keep him safe while he gains confidence. He has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be kind and understanding as he learns all about home life and new skills such as house training.

Otis doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and this will need to be introduced very gradually by practicing first in the garden, allowing him to gain confidence before venturing further afield.

Otis is a very worried boy who needs someone special to give him the time and understanding he deserves. With a calm environment, a confident canine companion and lots of patience and love, we hope that little by little he will begin to feel safe and discover the happy boy hiding underneath all those worries.

name: Tiny Tim
description:
I can live with older dog-savvy children who understand I need time to settle in.

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I would love a garden to run and play in!

I would love plenty of adventures once I am fully vaccinated!

I am just a puppy! Please be patient with me while I learn the basics!

Please read below for more information about my health!

03-11-26 Tiny Tim is a gorgeous and bouncy little pup who has come to us from a breeder. He is a lovely, happy boy who is always interested in what is going on around him and has been enjoying all the new experiences that come with living in a home. He has been spending time in a foster home and is showing us what a wonderful little companion he can be. He is a fairly chilled-out little chap who loves nothing more than a cuddle, a tummy rub and being close to his favourite people!

Tiny Tim has arrived with a Grade 3 left luxating patella and a Grade 4 right luxating patella. He has had X-rays which we are able to send to potential adopters for them to have checked at their own vets. Due to his diagnosis, he will need specialist surgery to help his mobility. Unfortunately, this cannot be carried out just yet as he is still growing, and it will need to be arranged once his growth plates have fused.

We would love to find adopters who are happy to welcome Tiny Tim into their lives as he is now and who would be able to fund his operation when he is old enough. It is estimated that this could cost around £3,000+, depending on which specialist is used, and it would not be covered by insurance as it is a pre-existing condition. We would love for him to settle into a forever home while he is still a puppy, where he can enjoy all the fun of growing up with his own family. If he isn't adopted during this time, we will continue to support him and arrange his surgery under our care once he is old enough.

Tiny Tim has been enjoying life in his foster home and has shown himself to be a lovely little house companion. He is quite happy pottering about, having little naps in his bed and keeping himself occupied with his toys, although he much prefers being curled up beside his foster mum and having his tummy rubbed! He loves attention and is very generous with his kisses, even if he has been told his breath could do with a little improvement! He is also quite the little snorer and has earned himself the nickname of an 'iPad kid' because he loves sitting peacefully watching things move on a screen.

He is currently living with another dog and enjoys having company, although he can sometimes find a bigger, more playful dog a little overwhelming. He is happy to retreat to his foster mum for reassurance when he needs a break. Tiny Tim can live with a suitable resident dog in his new home, provided they are happy to have a playful puppy around, or he could be the only dog where his adopters have plenty of time to spend with him. He can live with sensible, dog-savvy children who understand his needs.

Tiny Tim has been getting out and about for some short lead walks and is slowly getting used to wearing his harness. His back legs can be a little wobbly and his mobility does need to be considered, but this certainly doesn't stop him from enjoying life! He can be quite adventurous and sometimes forgets that his legs need a little extra care, so his adopters will need to be mindful of this and manage his activity carefully. He isn't particularly keen on travelling in the car as it can make him feel sick, and loud noises can worry him, so he will need some gentle reassurance with these things.

As Tiny Tim is still just a pup, he will need to continue learning all about the rules of home life, including house training and walking nicely on a lead. His adopters will need to be patient and willing to help him grow into a happy and confident little boy. His adopters will need to agree to have him neutered when he is old enough, and his family will need to take him to puppy socialisation and training as he grows.

Tiny Tim is such a gorgeous little character who has already experienced so many firsts and is thoroughly enjoying discovering the world around him. He is a loving, cuddly and sometimes cheeky little boy who deserves a family who will adore him, understand his medical needs and be there for him throughout his journey.

Day 39 of living in a foster home with Holly, home with Holly in the evenings and socialising with humans and other doggies during the days! As cool as that is I’m sure I’d love to have a home to call my own. I have been told I’m a chill dude, I nap and cuddle and show everyone my belly for fuss, I don’t like the car it makes me sick and loud noises scare me, but Holly keeps me safe and feeds me a lot. I have a room mate, she’s a lot bigger than me and sometimes squashes me when I try to play, but Holly is always there so I run to cuddle her when it gets too much. She likes to keep me safe in my crate when she has to leave the room but I miss her a lot so I break out, I hope my new home can keep up with my magic tricks because I’ve gotten quite good at it. When Holly is busy doing human things around the home I nap in my bed keeping myself out of trouble, I nibble my toys occasionally but I much prefer pulling on Hollys hair when I get the chance. I stay close to Holly but will keep out of the way and watch from a distance if she’s having zoomies in the kitchen.

I have been told my breath stinks but that doesn’t stop me giving everyone kisses and that I snore. But Holly won’t complain because I’m the quietest boy she’s ever met. We have been out exploring every now and then, I have to wear this suit…I think it’s called a harness? I don’t like it but if it means I get to spend more time with the humans let’s go! We have done some lead walks but only short ones, I’ve got wobbly back legs so sometimes they slow me down but not by a lot. I have beds scattered around the home but I take every opportunity to lay next to Holly even on her lap for some tummy rubs. I love it! I get carried around like a baby sometimes because it means I get more tummy rubs.

Holly has called me an ‘iPad kid’ it started when we’d watch things moving on a screen and I’d sit peacefully watching it move.

Holly took me to a new vet, they put me in this big box for an X-ray. I behaved myself and watched all the other people and doggies moving around the vets from the comfort of Hollys lap (my favourite place) don’t be fooled by my wobbly legs, I forget about them a lot and try to jump up and down off the furniture, I get zoomies like any other dog, I’m curious and maybe one day my legs will not be noticed, I’ve had a few first at the rescue I even had my first Halloween at the rescue with Holly and friends and met some new friends!

Holly’s hope for me is a loving home not just for Christmas but for all the care I need, and the promise that loving me will be the greatest gift you’ll ever receive

Tiny Tim is a gorgeous and bouncy little pup who has come to us from a breeder. He is a lovely, happy boy who is always ready to see what is going on around him and would make a wonderful addition to a loving and happy family who are ready to welcome him with open arms.

Tiny Tim has arrived with a Grade 3 left luxating patella, and a Grade 4 right luxating patella. He has had x-rays which we are able to send to potential adopters for them to have checked at their own vets. Due to the diagnosis, he will need to undergo specialist surgery to help his mobility. Unfortunately, this surgery cannot be carried out at the moment as he is so young and it will need to be done once he is older as soon as his growth plates have fused.

We would love to find adopters who are happy to welcome Tiny Tim into their lives as he is now and who would be able to fund his operation when he is old enough. It's estimated that it would cost around £3000+ depending on which specialist you use and would not be covered by insurance as it's a pre-existing condition. It would be wonderful for him to settle into a loving forever home while he is still a puppy, so he can enjoy all the joys of puppyhood and get to know his new family. If he isn’t adopted during this time, we will continue to support him and arrange the surgery under our care once he is old enough.

Tiny Tim can live with a resident dog in his new home, provided they don't mind having this playful little guy around. He could also be the only dog in a home where his adopters have plenty of time to spend with him and help him learn all about life in a home. As Tiny Tim is still just a pup, he will need to learn all of the house rules, including house training and walking nicely on a lead, so his new family will need to be patient and willing to help him learn.

His adopters will also need to agree to have him neutered when he is old enough and take him to plenty of puppy socialisation and training classes. These will be really important in helping Tiny Tim grow into a happy, confident and well-rounded adult.

Tiny Tim is a gorgeous little boy with lots of fun and love to give, and he is now ready to start his journey into the wonderful world of being someone's much-loved pet!

name: Kismet
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

I am spayed and have had an umbilical hernia repaired.

Kismet is a lovely girl who came to us from a breeder and has now moved to a wonderful foster home, where she is experiencing life in a home for the very first time. She has a sweet, gentle nature and is a curious, active little girl who is slowly finding her feet and learning that the world isn't such a scary place.

Kismet is still a little unsure of people, but she is making a lovely start in foster. She enjoys following her fosterer around and is happy to accept a gentle fuss, although she isn't quite brave enough to ask for attention herself just yet. She is beginning to settle into her new routine and sleeps quietly overnight snuggled up in a crate with her foster buddy, greeting her fosterer each morning with a lovely waggy tail. These little moments show that she is trying her best, and with time, patience and kindness, we hope she will continue to grow in confidence.

Kismet takes great comfort from the company of other dogs and will need a kind, friendly resident dog of a similar size in her new home. She would love a canine companion who enjoys snuggling up and sharing their bed, as having other dogs around helps her feel safe and secure while she gets used to her new surroundings.

Kismet is doing well with her toilet training when given regular opportunities to go out into the garden. She has also started learning to wear a harness, but she will need more time to build her confidence before beginning to learnt to walk on a lead, which can initially be introduced gently in the garden when she feels ready.

Kismet arrived with us very underweight, so she is currently being fed three meals a day in a crate to ensure she gets all the food she needs without her canine friends helping themselves! It will be important for her to continue enjoying a nutritious diet in her new home to help her reach and maintain a healthy weight. She also had a small umbilical hernia, which was repaired at the time of her spay.

As this is Kismet's first experience of living in a home, she will need patient adopters who understand that everything is new to her and who will give her the time and encouragement she needs to settle at her own pace. She will also need someone around for most of the day while she adjusts to her new routine, with any time left alone introduced gradually as she becomes more confident. Kismet can live with sensible, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who will understand her need for patience and reassurance.

Kismet is making a lovely start in foster and has so much potential to blossom into a happy, confident little companion. With a loving family, a reassuring canine friend and plenty of patience, we hope she will continue to discover just how wonderful life in a home can be and find the forever home she deserves.

Kismet has been given the Gift of Life by Margaret Hunter

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

Kismet has made a good start in foster. She has a sweet gentle nature, is curious, active, shadows her fosterer and sleeps quietly at night with her foster buddy Kylie in a crate, and greets me in the morning with a lovely waggy tail.

Kismet is underweight and is fed 3 meals a day in a crate so that she doesn’t allow the rest of the pack to help her out. With regular visits to the garden she is doing well with toilet training.

Harness training has started but lead walking will wait until she is more confident and then start in the garden. Kismet will accept a gentle fuss but does not ask for attention yet.

Kismet needs a home with at least one similar size playmate who likes to cosy up and share their bed as she takes great comfort from their presence and owners where someone is around most of the time while she settles into a new routine. Time alone will have to be built up gradually.

Kismet is a lovely, happy girl who has come into our care from a breeder. She is a semi-brave little girl who wants to be our friend, but just can't quite get there yet. If we need to pick her up, Kismet will lie down and accept the handling, and she will offer little kisses on our hands while wagging her tail. These small signs show that she is trying her best, even though she is still a little unsure.

Kismet gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles in and finds her paws.

As Kismet has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to give her plenty of time, patience and encouragement while she gets used to her new surroundings. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who are sensible and will allow her time to settle in.

Kismet has arrived very underweight, so she will need a nutritious diet to help her reach and maintain a healthy weight. This will need to be continued in her new home. She also has a small umbilical hernia, which has been repaired at the time of her spay.

Kismet is a sweet little girl who is clearly trying hard to be brave, and we hope that with the support of a kind canine companion and a loving, patient family, she will slowly gain confidence and discover just how lovely life in a home can be.
