name: Hooper
description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am neutered and have had an entropion repaired on my left eye.

Hooper is a very handsome gentleman who has come to us from a breeder. He was quite a nervous boy when he first arrived, but he has come on leaps and bounds and is now really starting to show us his lovely, bouncy personality! He gets so excited to see his familiar people in the mornings and has discovered that he absolutely loves a fuss. He will even paw at you for more attention once he has decided you're one of his favourites!

Hooper has become much more comfortable with handling and is now happy having his jumper put on and taken off. He can still be a little sensitive about having his legs touched, so this is something his adopters will need to continue working on gently, particularly to help with future grooming. He mixes wonderfully with other dogs and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in his new home to keep him company and help him settle.

Hooper has also made great progress with his walking and is now walking on a harness and lead! This is still quite new to him, and he can occasionally get spooked, but he is trying so hard to be brave. His adopters will need to continue building his confidence with gentle encouragement and positive experiences.

Hooper has never lived in a home before, so he will need patient adopters to help him learn about house training and all the new routines of family life. He can live with sensible, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ and will need adopters with previous ex-breeding experience who understand that he may need a little time to adjust.

Once Hooper has had his morning zoomies, he is quite a laid-back chap who would much rather curl up in a big, cosy bed and have a snooze! He arrived quite thin and shaved but has gained weight and grown a lovely thicker coat. His previously repaired left eye has also healed well following his entropion surgery.

Hooper really is a lovely boy who has made so much progress and deserves a home of his own. He is a typical Poodle who loves fuss, other dogs and his comfy beds, and we think he will make a wonderful companion for a family who can give him the love and sofa spot he deserves!

Hooper has been given the Gift of Life by Jackie Coleman

Hooper has come on leaps and bounds over the last month since being with us. He has really started coming out of his shell and showing his bouncy personality. In the mornings he gets so excited to see me now, it’s worlds apart from the dog weeks ago who couldn’t wait for me to leave his kennel!

Hooper has discovered he loves fuss and will paw at me for more. He was very touch shy to start with but with his familiar people he loves a fuss. Getting his jumper on and off was a challenge at the start but now it’s easy for us to do! Hooper is still a little sensitive about being touched on his legs but we are slowly working on desensitising this to aid future grooming.

Hooper also now walks on a harness/ lead! It’s still fairly new to him & he can get spooked sometimes but he’s trying his best to be brave! Once he’s had his zoomies he’s quite a laid back dog & loves a comfy, cozy bed to curl up in. After his morning zoomies he’d much rather stay in bed where it’s warm! He is respect of his bedding & loves big comfy beds, especially with the weather starting to turn.

Hooper arrived to us quite thin & shaved but has got a thicker coat & has gained some weight too! His eye has healed well too!Hooper mixes well with other dogs & really is a poodle lovers dream! Whilst he’s doing well with us here, what Hooper deserves is a home to call his own & a spot on the sofa so he can be treated like royalty. (a life I think he’ll settle into quickly).

Hooper is a very handsome gentleman who has come to us from a breeder. He can be a little on the nervous side, especially when meeting new people, but he is growing in confidence every day and we are beginning to see more of his lovely personality. Hooper is starting to trust the familiar faces he sees regularly, although he can still be unsure when someone new approaches him and may retreat to the back of his kennel where he feels safest.

Hooper shares his kennel wonderfully with his doggy friends and really enjoys having them around him. He will need at least one calm and confident resident dog in his new home that he can lean on and look to for reassurance as he continues to build his confidence. Having a friendly dog by his side will be a big help to Hooper as he learns that the world isn't such a scary place.

Hooper can live with older, sensible, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16+ who understand that he is a nervous boy and will give him the time and space he needs to settle in. He isn't walking on a lead yet, so his adopters will need to be patient as he learns this new skill. For Hooper, some quiet garden sniffs may be the perfect place to start while he gets used to his new surroundings before gradually building up to adventures further afield.

Hooper has never lived in a home before, so there will be lots for him to learn. His adopters will need to be kind and patient as he learns about house training and all the new sights, sounds, routines and experiences that come with home life. He will need someone who understands that his progress may take time and who will allow him to move at his own pace without putting pressure on him.

Hooper will need adopters with previous ex-breeding experience who understand the patience and understanding these dogs can require. He isn't going to be the sort of dog who walks straight into a new home and feels completely at ease, but we know that with the right person, he has the potential to make some amazing progress.

Hooper really needs someone to take a chance on him and show him just how wonderful life can be. He is a gentle boy who is slowly learning to trust, and we hope that the right family will see the lovely dog underneath his nerves and give him the time, patience and love he deserves.

He has had an entropion repaired on his left eye.

name: Bee
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teens who respect my space.

I would like to be homed with another canine friend. I've not met cats so I'm unsure!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Bee is a gentle, shy little lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is still a timid girl who can find the world around her a little overwhelming, but she has been making some lovely progress since arriving with us and is really trying hard to be brave.

Bee can be handled and picked up as long as you take things slowly and carefully. She is beginning to show us that she wants to build a bond with people, and she has started getting very excited to see her favourite people in the mornings, running over to say hello and even giving little kisses on their fingers! She is still a little unsure about accepting fusses, but we think she is getting closer to letting her guard down and learning that human attention can be a lovely thing.

Bee has always lived with the company of other dogs and gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends. She relies on their company for comfort and reassurance, so she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can learn from, follow and look to as she settles into home life. We think having a friendly dog or two around will really help her find her confidence and make the transition into a home much easier.

Bee has never lived in a home before, so there is still lots for her to learn. She has recently had her first little introduction to wearing a harness and did brilliantly! Although she only managed a few steps, she was happy to have a sniff around, take some treats and explore without becoming overwhelmed. We will continue building on this little by little, and her adopters will need to be patient as she learns about lead walking, house training and all the other things that come with home life.

Bee will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with worried ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need time to settle and gain confidence at her own pace. We think she will really benefit from being away from the busy kennel environment and having the chance to learn about life in a quieter setting. She can live with sensible teenagers who understand that she will need to be given space and allowed to settle without pressure.

Bee is such a little sweetheart, and it is lovely to see her starting to show us the happy little girl hiding underneath all those worries. She is trying so hard to be brave, and we think she has so much potential to blossom in the right home. With an experienced ex-breeding dog home, kind canine companions to guide her and plenty of love and reassurance, we are sure Bee will make a wonderful addition to the family. Please don't keep this lovely girl waiting any longer for her chance at home life!

Bee has been at the rescue for just about a month now and I love her more and more every day. She’s still a timid little girl, but I can tell she’s trying so hard to be brave. She gets really excited to see me in the mornings and will run up to me and give me kisses on my fingers, and it’s so sweet to see. I think she really wants to start having fusses from me, but she’s still holding back just that little bit. I really don’t think it will take too long for her to drop her guard though!! And I do also think she’ll come on a lot faster in a quiet home environment as opposed to busy kennels!

Today I took her out on a harness for the first time. She didn’t take many steps, but she did some sniffs, took treats off me, and didn’t have any panics. To me, this is a brilliant first attempt!!! I only did a very short session as I didn’t want to overwhelm her, so I’ll keep doing that little by little and I do think she’ll start to walk relatively soon. I’m not saying she’s going to be a pro walking up mountains any time soon, but baby steps!Bee is SUCH a little sweetheart and she’s really no bother to look after at the rescue at all. I think she’ll slot into home life pretty quickly with a sibling or 2 to help her. So please don’t keep her waiting much longer.

Bee is a gentle, shy little lady who has come into our care from a breeder alongside her sister, Gemma. She has been making great progress since coming to us, although she is still a very timid girl who is feeling overwhelmed by many aspects of the world around her.

Bee can be handled and picked up as long as you take things slowly and carefully. She still finds human interaction worrying, so her adopters will need to give her plenty of time and patience to build trust and understand that people can be kind and positive.

Bee has always lived with the company of other dogs and gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends. She relies on their company for comfort, so she will need a kind, confident resident dog in her new home who she can learn from, follow and look to for reassurance as she settles into home life.

Bee has never lived in a home before, so there is lots for her to learn. She will need patient adopters who understand that lead training, toilet training and all the other basics of home life will be completely new to her. She does not yet have these skills and will need them introduced gradually, with plenty of encouragement and positive reinforcement.

Bee will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with worried ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need time to settle and gain confidence at her own pace. She can live with teenagers who are sensible and understand that she will need to be given space and allowed to settle without pressure.

Bee is a really lovely girl who is trying hard to find her confidence. She deserves a home who will absolutely adore her and give her all the time, patience and reassurance she needs. With an experienced ex-breeding dog home, a kind resident dog to guide her and plenty of love, we are sure Bee will continue to blossom into a very sweet addition to the family.

name: Nora
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I’m new to walking on a harness and doing well!

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

Nora is a gentle girl who has come to us from a breeder and is now in foster, where she has been able to experience life in a home for the first time. She has been in foster for over a month now, and this has given us a much better understanding of her mobility, as well as allowing her confidence to grow and her lovely personality to shine through.

Nora is still very mistrustful of people, but she is beginning to show us that she really does want to make friends. She is now much more willing to approach her fosterer and has recently started coming over to take treats from her. She will even jump up onto the sofa to watch Netflix, as long as there is another dog already on the sofa with her! These may seem like small things, but for Nora they are huge steps forward and show just how much she is beginning to relax. She will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her home that will allow her to lean on them as she continues to settle.

She absolutely loves the comforts of home life and takes great reassurance from having other dogs around her. She has also been on a few short walks outside the home, allowing her to slowly experience the world beyond her garden. She is still a very sensitive girl and everything will need to be introduced gradually, but she is making lovely progress.

Nora's mobility has also improved in a home setting. Her ataxia appears to be closely linked to her stress levels and is much more noticeable when she is worried or overwhelmed. When she is relaxed, her movements are almost normal, which is incredibly encouraging. She is not currently on any medication, and her fosterer is helping her to build muscle strength through daily massage and gentle exercise.

Nora will need a quiet and understanding home with adopters who have experience with nervous dogs and, ideally, ex-breeders. She will need at least one calm, friendly resident dog to give her confidence and show her the way. Her new family will need to be incredibly patient and allow her to settle and build trust at her own pace, without expecting too much too soon.

Nora has had lots of hardships in her life and is still learning that she can feel safe around people. However, the progress she has made since moving into foster has been wonderful to see. Beneath her worries is a very sweet girl who is slowly discovering how lovely life can be, and we are hoping that the right home will give her the security, patience and love she needs to continue blossoming.

Nora has been given the Gift of Life by Judie Fisher

Nora has been in foster for over a month now which allowed us to have a good assessment of her mobility, and also helped increase her confidence and introduce her to living in a home. This gentle girl has a very sweet personality and loves the comforts of home life and the company of other dogs. She is still very mistrustful of humans, but I can see that she is now more willing to try and be friends. She has recently started coming up to take a treat from me, and will even jump up on the sofa to watch Netflix with me (as long as there is another dog on the sofa too). She has also been on a few short walks outside to see the world beyond my home and garden!

Nora's ataxia has improved in a home setting too, largely because it is connected to her mental state and seems to be worse when she is stressed. When Nora is relaxed, her movements are almost normal, which is lovely to see and gives me hope that once she feels safe and comfortable mentally, she will have a great quality of life. We just need to help her get there. Nora is not on any medication at the moment, but I massage her daily and we are working on building her muscle strength.

Nora's ideal home will be a quiet setting with one or more calm and friendly dogs. Her people will need to be kind and very patient, with experience of scared dogs and preferably beagles too. This gorgeous girl has had lots of hardships in her life, it is time for her to finally have a place where she feels safe and loved.

I have been working with Nora a few days a week since she first arrived with us and was on medication and crate rest for her legs. Around two weeks ago, Nora moved to a different section, so I haven't seen her in a little while. I popped over today to check in and chat to one of her new kennel dads to see how she's doing.

Since arriving on her new section, Nora has made huge leaps! She is now harness-trained and wears her harness comfortably during the day. She has grown more confident with handling and with walking on her harness to and from the yard, though she is not yet feeling up to walks outside the centre. She also now sits curiously at the front of her kennel, watching people and dogs come and go on her section, rather than hiding in the back.

Nora still has a long way to go in learning to trust humans and receive our love, but she's made huge steps already. It's a great reminder that all of us working here have different skills, and sometimes a dog who is struggling just needs a change of scene to take the next steps in their journey towards their forever home.

Nora is so gentle and if you ignore the deep defensive howl (she is a beagle after all!) eventually she quietens down and she shows her soft side.Nora is still trying to get used to enjoying human company. She is not there yet but is slowly beginning to show signs of trusting people and does settle near you with a little patience.

It appears to me that it's not that Nora dislikes people, it's more a matter of how she is unsure of who we are and how we do things.

Once she  settles and it does take a little time, although still afraid, is much more willing to be approached by people.

In this calmer state, I was able to smooth her coat all over and gently stroke her without her worrying too much which is a positive step for her.

Nora will need this gentle approach for some time but the reward will be endless love and loyalty which is priceless.

I believe all Nora needs right now is the stability and security that a loving home can offer.Nora does much prefer the company of dogs  at the moment so it is a must that there is a resident dog already in the home for her to be with.

Nora has kennelled with small dogs but we do feel she would be better placed with a dog of a similar size or larger.

Our next step whilst Nora is with us will be to train her to walk on a harness so she can start to discover and enjoy the outside world.

Nora has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a very special forever home. She is a scared girl who is understandably feeling overwhelmed to find herself here and is desperately in need of kindness, patience and TLC as she begins to settle and learn that the world can be a safe place.

When Nora first arrived with us, she was showing some neurological symptoms and ataxia, and her back legs would occasionally slide from underneath her, causing her to stumble. Following investigations with our vets, it was found that her proprioception was delayed in all four limbs. She was trialed on a course of medication alongside crate rest and has made wonderful progress. Her proprioception is now normal, she is able to get around and play happily, and she enjoys life much more comfortably. She does still have a slight amount of ataxia and can occasionally limp still. Our vet feels that she may have suffered an acute injury at some point in the past which has largely resolved itself, though she will likely never present like a normal dog.

Nora will be looking for adopters who will love and cherish her just as she is. Due to her mobility history, she will need a home without slippery flooring, or one where plenty of rugs and runners are in place to help her move around confidently and safely.

She would be best suited to a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience of nervous ex-breeding dogs and understand her worries. Nora will need time to settle at her own pace and will thrive with patient adopters who are happy to let her progress in her own time. She takes great comfort from the company of other dogs and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to show her the way and help her build confidence.

Nora has never experienced life in a home before so her new family will need to be understanding as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She doesn't yet walk on a lead and harness and initially she will need to practise wearing her harness and exploring safely within the home and garden before she is ready to venture further afield.

Although Nora is still very worried and unsure of the world around her, beneath her fears is a sweet and deserving little girl who simply needs someone to believe in her. Watching a scared dog slowly learn to trust is one of the most rewarding experiences, and with love, patience and understanding, Nora will blossom. The day she greets you with a wagging tail and a sparkle in her eyes will make every moment of that journey worthwhile.

name: Tummy
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teenagers, aged 13+ who respect my space.

I will need to be the only dog in the home so all of the attention is on me!

I'd like a secure garden to potter around in.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have previously lived in a home, so I may already know the basics!

I am on a special diet for bladder stones, please read below for more information!

11-10-26 Tummy is a lovely lady who originally came to us from a breeder and was later adopted into a home. Sadly, she has returned to our care after around 5 months as she wasn't getting along with the resident dog, so she is now looking for a home where she can be the only dog and have all of her family's attention to herself. She also cannot live with cats or small furries.

Tummy is a sweet and outgoing girl with a big personality! She loves toys and having a good play, but she also enjoys a quiet fuss and relaxing alongside her people. She has lived in a home before, so she may already know some of the basics such as house training, although she may need a few gentle reminders as she settles back into home life.

Tummy would do best with a family who has experience with Dachshunds and understands their wonderful but sometimes strong personalities, although she could also live with a sensible family who are willing to learn and understand her needs. She can live with dog-savvy teenagers aged 13+ who are sensible and will give her the time and space she needs to settle into her new home.

Tummy has never been left home alone before and so this is something her adopters will need to build up gradually with her to ensure she doesn't develop separation anxiety.

Tummy is an amazing little lady who has already had a change of home and is now ready to find her forever family. We hope that the right home will give her the love, attention and stability she deserves.

Tummy has previously been treated for ear infections and also has some hair loss that seemed to begin to grow back when she was in her previous home. She has a history of bladder stones and is currently on a specific diet to help with this, and this will need to be continued in the home. This will need to be monitored by her new vets and her adopters will need to be aware that should she require any treatment or potential surgery in the future it would not be covered by insurance.

name: Fanta
description:
I can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who understand I need space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need a secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before

I've started my vaccinations and will be spayed before adoption.

22-10-26 Fanta is quite a scared girly who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is in need of lots of TLC and the reassurance of a confident resident dog to help her feel safe. Fanta can be a little panicky and flighty, so she will need a very secure garden with high fencing to keep her safe while she settles into her new surroundings.

Although Fanta was shaking, she allowed us to pick her up and give her a gentle fuss to reassure her that we are here to help. She is still very unsure at the moment, so her new family will need to be patient and allow her the time she needs to learn to trust.

Fanta will need another kind and confident dog in her new home, as this will be a much-needed support system for her. A reassuring canine companion can help guide her and give her the confidence she needs as she settles in and begins to find her paws.

As Fanta has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. Her adopters will need to understand that this may take time and be prepared to let her progress at her own pace. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who understand she needs time to settle in. Her adopters will need to have ex-breeding experience to better understand her needs.

Fanta is a very worried little girl, but she has already shown us that she can accept gentle affection even when she is feeling frightened. We hope that with a confident canine companion, a calm environment and lots of patience, she will gradually begin to feel safe and discover the happy new life she deserves.

description:

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

Kelsey has been caught climbing here at the rescue, so she will need a very secure garden with high, flat fencing to make sure she stays safe.

We believe that Kelsey will need another kind dog in her new home, and this dog will be a much-needed support system for her as she settles in and gets used to all the new experiences that come with home life. She can live with older, dog-savvy children who are sensible and understand she needs time to settle in.

As Kelsey has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to give her time, patience and encouragement while she learns. She has been known to climb at the rescue, and will need a fenced garden of at least 6ft that will keep her safe.

Kelsey is a sweet little girl who has already shown us that she can cope well with gentle handling, and we hope that with the support of a canine companion and a loving family, she will continue to grow in confidence and enjoy her happy new start.

name: Parker
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

Please be patient with me, I'm nervous and learning everything from scratch.

I will be neutered before finding my forever home! Read below for more!

01-10-26 Parker is a nervous boy who has come to us from a breeder. He is fine to handle but can be very unsure and will often try to hide away when he is approached. He is trying so hard to be brave, and we are sure that with the right person willing to take a chance on him, he will slowly learn that he has nothing to be afraid of.

Parker will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home and would benefit from adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and will allow him to settle in at his own pace. He will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in his new home who can take him under their wing and show him the ropes.

Parker has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be kind and patient as he learns all about home life, including house training and walking on a lead. These things may take some time, and his adopters will need to understand that he will need to progress at his own pace without being rushed.

Parker is a nervous boy at the moment, but underneath that uncertainty is a lovely boy who is trying his very best. With time, patience and a loving home willing to give him a chance, we hope to see Parker blossom into the wonderful companion we know he can be.

Parker is currently being treated for an ear infection.

name: Candy
description:
I would like a home filled with love and kindness!

I can live with larger, playful resident dogs, or I can be the only dog in the home!

I would like a large, and secure garden with 6ft+ fences.

I walk well on a lead, but I can be strong so my adopters will need to work with this

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home! Read below for more!

Candy is a very sweet and affectionate lady who has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for her forever home. She absolutely adores attention and cuddles and, once she gets to know you, it doesn't take her long to show just how loving she really is. Candy simply wants to be close to her people and has completely stolen the hearts of everyone she has met. She has blossomed into the most loving girl and will make a wonderful companion and is sure to become the ultimate cuddle bug in the home.

Candy has built a lovely bond with the staff member who has worked closely with her since she first arrived. She truly trusts her and has come on so much since arriving with us. Candy has such a sweet nature and it is clear how much she enjoys spending time with people she knows and trusts.

Her lead walking has improved so much too. She is now walking much better and really enjoys her outings, although her adopters will need to continue working on her lead manners so she can enjoy plenty of adventures.

Candy mixes well with polite, well mannered dogs however she can sometimes be a little selective with choosing her friends. She doesn’t appreciate when dogs are over the top but when she does make a new friend her own play style can be quite full on! She comes away when called so we are always able to calm her down for a tasty treat. Because of her size and excitable nature, she would not be able to live with smaller breeds of dogs in the home and will need a home without cats.

As Candy is a very large lady, it is important that her adopters have experience with a similar breed and understand her needs. We have found that she can be particularly worried by formal handling, such as veterinary examinations, and finds these situations quite stressful. We will be muzzle training Candy so that she can be safely and comfortably handled for occasions such as vet visits. She recently needed to visit the vet due to sore ears and, although she found having her ears examined uncomfortable, she coped very well with the support of people she knows and trusts. She did also need to visit the vet for a check up on a day when her regular person wasn't around and found it much harder to cope with and became extremely stressed and agitated. She takes so much comfort from her known and trusted people.

Candy would be best suited to an adult-only home where her adopters can give her the time and space she needs to build trust and settle in.

Candy has arrived with a scab on the right side of her face that will be addressed during the time of her spay and is being treated for a ear infection.

Candy has come such a long way since arriving with us and is now so ready for a loving home of her own. She is an absolute angel and a true credit to her breed, with so much love and affection to give. She truly deserves someone who will give her the love, patience and happiness she deserves.

Candy will need more than one meet and greet with her prospective adopters to allow her time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Candy has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

Candy has blossomed into the most loving and affectionate girl, and I genuinely love spending my days with her. She has such a sweet nature and has come on so much since arriving with us.

Candy recently had a vet visit due to having sore ears. Although you could tell she was uncomfortable while the vet was examining them, she was such a good girl throughout, and I was incredibly proud of her.

She has also mixed with quite a few dogs here at the rescue and has been brilliant with all of them. She can sometimes be a little bouncy and excitable when first meeting new dogs, but she listens when asked to calm down and is learning to manage her excitement really well.

Her lead walking has improved so much too, and she’s now walking much better and enjoying her outings.

Candy has come such a long way and is so ready for a loving home of her own. She truly deserves someone who will give her the love, patience and happiness she deserves.

She will make a wonderful companion and is sure to become the ultimate cuddle bug in the home.

Candy is an incredible girl, but she can be sensitive when she is worried or when she feels uncomfortable, for this reason, we feel she would be best suited to an adult-only home where her adopters can give her the time and space she needs to build trust and settle in.

name: Tippins
description:
I would like a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need another dog my size or larger in my new home.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk on lead but I can be spooked. Let's take it slow!

I have spent some time in a home, but still have lots to learn.

Tippins is a lovely lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She can be apprehensive when meeting new people and may bark at strangers, but once she feels comfortable, her wonderful personality shines through. She has formed lovely bonds with staff at the rescue and, once attached to someone, she adores cuddles and wants to be as close to her favourite people as possible. She is a ridiculously affectionate girl who gives her whole heart to those she trusts.

Tippins was briefly adopted as an only but has sadly returned to our care as she really struggled without another dog by her side. Although she didn't appear to rely on other dogs for comfort in kennels, she became very shut down in the home and struggled to come out of her shell. We therefore feel she will need a calm and confident resident dog, her size or larger, to act as a role model and help her settle. She isn't particularly cuddly with other dogs, but she shares her kennel well and we believe having another dog around will help her feel more secure while she adjusts to her new surroundings.

Tippins walks beautifully on her harness alongside her handler, although busy places and traffic can still make her nervous. Her new family should continue her confidence-building with quiet walks and plenty of reassurance.

Although she has spent some time in a home, Tippins had never experienced home life before her adoption and so her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she learns all about home life and house training. She will need a quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand that settling into a home may take her some time. Once she feels secure, she will try her very best to be brave and become a devoted companion.

Tippins can live with teenagers aged 16 and over who are sensible and able to respect her need for a gentle introduction. Her adopters should also be prepared to welcome her onto the furniture, as we suspect this affectionate girl will thoroughly enjoy being close to her people once she feels safe.

Tippins has returned to us with an ear infection and is currently receiving treatment. Our vets are monitoring her ears and will continue to provide any treatment she needs. She will need her ears to be monitored and cared for in her new home as appropriate.

Tippins is a very special little lady who has made fantastic progress with us. With the right canine role model, an experienced and peaceful home, and the time she needs to settle, we hope she will finally discover just how wonderful life can be.

Tippins has been with me for about a month now, and I have really, REALLY fallen for her. Even though she presents as a nervous girl and will bark at strangers, it doesn’t take her long to let her guard down at all. When she does, she is your best friend, your shadow, your snuggle buddy... and you are her whole world. She absolutely adores the people she loves and really gives her whole heart to us. She is ridiculously affectionate, and I fear she’s so wasted being in kennels.

Tippins walks beautifully on a harness right by my side and looks up at me to check in constantly. She can still be nervous in busy places and around traffic, but that is something that she’ll get used to in time. I would recommend her adopters do some practice in the garden first before they venture out, and definitely establish a bond with her first.

Even though Tippins has never been in a home before, I’m pretty certain she’s going to want to join everyone on the furniture for snuggles, so this must be welcomed with open arms. Every day with me, she jumps up onto the bench next to me in the play yard, and she loves it when I sit in her bed in her kennel with her. So she’s a cuddler for sure!!

Please don’t keep this very special girl waiting for too much longer. She deserves to be loved and in a home so much.

Tippins is a lovely lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is a little apprehensive when she first meets new people, but she is already showing signs that her confidence is growing. Once she knows you, she enjoys a fuss and is happy to be handled. Tippins has a big personality and is a fun girl to spend time with.At the moment, Tippins is feeling a little less brave and is finding comfort in the company of her kennel friends. We feel it would be best for her to be rehomed with at least one other confident resident dog for support and companionship. She has always lived with bigger dogs and seems happiest around them. Tippins can be a little bossy with less confident dogs, so she wouldn't be suitable to live with smaller or younger dogs. We will continue to assess her confidence while she is with us to see if she could adapt to being an only dog. She will need adopters with ex-breeding experience that can understand her needs.As Tippins has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. Her new family will need to be patient while she settles in and learns what home life is all about. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens, aged 16+ that can allow her time to settle into a calm environment.Tippins already walks on a lead, but doesn't seem to be overly confident on this so she will need continued support as she learns, and once she has settled into her new home, she would enjoy one or two walks around the local area with her resident dog so that she can continue lead training.Tippins is a lovely girl with lots of character. She's already showing us what a sweet dog she is, and we hope that, with time and patience, she'll continue to grow in confidence and enjoy everything home life has to offer.Tippins is now receiving regular cleanings from the vets for waxy ears and this will need to be monitored in her new home.

name: Archie
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been neutered and have had 21 teeth removed.

Archie is such a sweet little man who came into our care from a breeder. He was adopted but has sadly been returned after his adopters felt they were not the right match for him. Archie formed a very strong bond with his female owner, but found it much harder to build a relationship with her husband, who was frequently away from home and therefore had very little opportunity to gain Archie's trust. When Archie becomes closely bonded to his favourite person, he can become protective of them. In his previous home, he nipped when he was sitting with his owner and her husband approached, so his new adopters will need to understand this behaviour and be prepared to continue building his confidence in a positive and patient way.

He is a cuddly and affectionate little dog once he feels comfortable, although he isn't quite brave enough to take treats from our hands just yet. Although Archie gets on well with other dogs, he can become protective of his favourite person around them, so we think he would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where he can relax and build a close bond with his new family.

As Archie has lived in a home before, he will already be familiar with the sights and sounds of home life. However, he may need a little reminding of his house training in a new environment. He walks well on a lead and enjoys his walks with volunteers.

Archie is looking for a quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of the breed and of rescue dogs. He will need people who are happy to give him the time and space he needs to settle and understand that he is safe.

Archie is doing really well since returning to us and his confidence is growing all the time. He is such a loving little dog, and in the right home, we hope he will continue to thrive and become a devoted companion.

We absolutely love this little guy at the rescue, Archie may be small but his personality is mighty. He is funny, lovable and impossible not to love. Archie is still a tiny bit shy with new people but it’s taking him less and less time to open up to new people and dogs. Archie loves to play with tennis balls, smother you with kisses and generally amuse us with his cheeky personality. Archie would like a child-free home as he is still a little anxious at times.

Archie is an absolute pleasure to work with! It’s been some time now, and our bond continues to grow stronger every day.He absolutely loves smothering you with kisses and will do anything to get himself onto your lap! Archie has been kennelled with a few dogs and socialised with plenty more, but he has become particularly taken with a Cocker called Trixie. They share some similar traits, including not wanting to share their humans, although neither has displayed any jealousy towardsthe other so far. They absolutely love running laps around the yard together before heading straight into your lap for some fuss. Archie will even stand on Trixie’s back just to make sure he gets in on the action and doesn’t miss out on any attention!As mentioned, Archie is yet to display any jealous traits towards either dogs or humans, but that doesn’t mean he won’t potentially show this once settled into a home. It’s something any potential adopter should be mindful of and prepared to manage appropriately.

What I can promise, though, is that Archie will become your best friend. He has so much love to give and, once he trusts you, he will love you unconditionally.This gorgeous boy deserves someone who will give him the love, patience and understanding he needs — and in return, you’ll have a loyal companion who will want nothing more than to be by your side.

Archie is the funniest and cheekiest of little Dachshunds. Archie needs a little time to warm to you (but not all that long), and once he does, he is the most lovely of boys. I have been caring for him for a few weeks now, and I am totally smitten.

Archie walks beautifully on lead and loves nothing more than when we venture out for a stroll along the lanes around the rescue. Archie is very fond of his toys and will happily run around the yard with a ball in his mouth. He will also spend much time organising his cuddly toys, making sure they are in just the right place.

Archie has been kennelled with other small female dogs. He seems to do best with robust smaller females, as he can be a little frisky with the more timid dogs. Archie could go as an only dog in the right home, one where there are humans who will have lots of time for him.

Archie is very enthusiastic with his kisses once he knows you and will desperately clamber over you for fusses. Archie is an all-round lovely little dog, best suited to a quiet adult home where there is plenty of love, time, and patience for him to truly settle in.

Archie formed a very strong bond with his female owner, but found it much harder to build a relationship with her husband, who was frequently away from home and therefore had very little opportunity to gain Archie's trust. When Archie becomes closely bonded to his favourite person, he can become protective of them. In his previous home, he nipped when he was sitting with his owner and her husband approached, so his new adopters will need to understand this behaviour and be prepared to continue building his confidence in a positive, patient way.

He is a cuddly, affectionate little dog once he feels comfortable, although he isn't quite brave enough to take treats from our hands just yet. Although Archie gets on well with other dogs, he can become protective of his favourite person around them, so we think he would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where he can relax and build a close bond with his new family.

Archie is a gorgeous little boy who came to us from a breeder and was understandably unsure of the world around him. It was truly heartbreaking to see how frightened he was as he would shy away from human contact and retreat when approached. Archie needs gentle handling, patience, and calm, slow movements to help him feel safe. Already, we are seeing progress. He enjoys a gentle fuss and has grown some confidence wagging his tail enthusiastically.

He gains reassurance from other dogs and will need a kind, confident resident dog in his new home to help guide him, boost his confidence, and show him that people and home life can be safe and rewarding.

Archie has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be patient and understanding as he learns the basics, including house training and walking on a lead. He could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over, who can appreciate and understand that he will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and his own space to settle in.

Since arriving with us, Archie has undergone extensive and much-needed dental treatment and has had 21 teeth removed. He is now recovering well and feeling much more comfortable.

name: Crispin
description:
I would like a calm and quiet home where I can settle in.

I would prefer to be the only dog in the home. I don't mind cats!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and love being out and about!

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

Crispin originally came to us from a breeder last October. He was adopted for a few months but returned to our care after his adopters sadly realised they were not the right match for him. Although they gave him every opportunity to settle, Crispin remained very worried whenever the male in the household was home and struggled to relax in his company.

Since returning to us, Crispin has moved into foster and has settled beautifully. He is an incredibly loving, cuddly little boy who simply wants to be close to his people. While he can initially be worried by some men, his foster carer has found that once visitors give him some attention, he quickly relaxes and happily cuddles up with them. He does the same with female visitors. He has adult grandsons in his foster home and, after an initial bark, is very happy to settle down with them.

Crispin does get on with other dogs, but he can be quite keen to push his way in for attention and may grumble if another dog gets in the way. He is not aggressive and, having no teeth, cannot bite, but he would be best suited to being homed as an only dog. His foster carer feels he would particularly enjoy being the centre of his person's world, as he simply loves being with his human, male or female.

Crispin absolutely loves his walks and this is his favourite pastime. He gets wonderfully excited when it is time to go out and walks beautifully on both a lead and harness. He is sociable with other dogs he meets, enjoys exploring new places and travels well in the car. He particularly loves visiting the coffee shop and is happiest when he can be out and about with his people.

As Crispin has now experienced life in a home, he has settled well into a routine and sleeps soundly through the night. He has had the occasional wee indoors first thing in the morning, although this has been improving, so his adopters should continue his house training with patience and consistency.

Crispin forms incredibly strong bonds with his favourite people and loves to be close by and involved in everything they are doing. He showed signs of separation anxiety in his previous home when left for more than a couple of hours, so his ideal home would be one where someone is around for most of the day and any time alone can be built up gradually.

Crispin has a cataract in his right eye and is developing one in his left. Despite this, he gets around brilliantly and you would hardly know he has eyesight problems. He has also had all of his teeth removed and will need to remain on a soft diet for life. He has Grade 2 patella luxation in both hind legs, which may continue to improve with gentle exercise as

Crispin has a travel document, which says he is 7 years old, but we do feel he could potentially be a little older than this.

Crispin has been given the Gift of Life by Katrina Pirner

Crispin is looking for his own special human where he can be the ONLY dog and have all the love and affection for himself. Although he is in foster with other dogs, we think he would now prefer to be the only dog in the home.

Crispin has recently spent a few days with another fosterer as I was on holiday and attached himself to the lady of the house and wasn't interested in the other 5 dogs or man of the house just the lady.

He walks perfectly on the lead and loves to go out as many times as you're willing to take him, equally though he loves to potter in the garden alongside his fosterer whilst she's raking up leaves. He loves to settle inside either on your lap or close by on the sofa.

Crispin enjoys all foods though some treats have to be in small pieces as he has no teeth but he eats either wet food or kibble with warm water to mash it down. His cataract doesn't affect him at all. Although Crispin is 7 he has the energy and zest for life of a much younger dog. He can literally walk for hours.

Crispin would love a one person, male or female, calm household where he can soak up all the attention from his special human. Although he gets on with all dogs outside of the home, he prefers to be cuddled up with his human wherever it may be.. sofa, bed he s not fussed as long as he knows they are close by him.

Crispin walks perfectly on a harness and lead and is good off lead too. He will walk ahead of you but keep coming back to 'check in' with you.

Crispin continues to thrive in his foster home and is loving this home life. He loves his food, loves his walks, loves his cuddles and just loves everything to be honest.

Although Crispin lives alongside his foster sisters, I do feel he would love a home with no other dogs and just a single active  adult home, male or female, where he can have all the attention and love. Cats are fine, as he dosen't take any notice of them.

Although his initial write states that he may be older than 7 I feel he is aged about right apart from his lack of teeth as he is full of energy and  fun.

Crispin is smashing this home life. He is an absolute gentleman and will make a perfect best friend for an active person who is at home most of the time.

This week he has visited various secure fields, visited coffee shops and even popped into a pub for a cool drink while out on a street walk. He loves to be out and about with his human and then return home for snuggles on the sofa.

Although Crispin has a cataract in his right eye this does not seem to affect him at all. His luxating patellas also don't seem to bother him and his movement is 100%.

Crispin recently moved foster homes through no fault of his own. He is a gorgeous, well mannered, cuddly boy who loves his walks, his humans and his food.

He gets along with the cats and dogs in my home, though initially Crispin demanded all the attention and would push the other dogs out of the way to get his cuddles first but with careful handling this has improved over the week.

He loves to cuddle up on my bed with my own dogs and sleeps all night there. He lives for his walks and gets very excited when his lead/harness appear. He can walk on his own or with another dog for company.

He happily shares his food bowl with his foster friend Lemon Pie. Even the cats dig in with him sometimes. He is getting used to being left when I go shopping and I am extending these trips so he gets used to being without humans for a while. Crispin does bark initially when visitors come into my home but this soon subsides when he realises they will do him no harm. Keep up the good work Crispin, you've got this my boy

Crispin has been back in foster care for a week and has settled in beautifully. He is an incredibly loving, cuddly little boy who simply wants to be loved. Sadly, he was returned because he became anxious and barked whenever the man in the household moved around.

He walks beautifully on a lead and harness, sleeps soundly through the night alongside the other foster dog, and travels well. Although he is perfectly happy living with other dogs, he could also be an only dog so he can enjoy all the cuddles and affection he deserves. He has had a few little accidents indoors first thing in the morning, but over the last few days he has settled into a much better routine.

Crispin has no teeth, so he will need to remain on a soft diet for the rest of his life. He also has a cataract in one eye and the beginnings of a cataract in the other, but you would hardly know he has any sight issues as he gets around so well.

He really is a very special little boy who simply needs a loving home where he can feel safe, secure, and cherished.

Crispin originally came to us from a breeder last October. He was adopted for a few months but has come back into our care after his adopters sadly realised they were not the right match for him. Although they gave him every opportunity to settle, Crispin remained very worried whenever the male in the household was home and simply couldn't relax in his company.Crispin is a dear little boy who can still be worried and unsure at times. It is clear that he had very little socialisation in the past, and although he has made lovely progress since living in a home, he still needs patient adopters who understand that building trust takes time. He can be touch-sensitive when he is feeling anxious, so gentle handling and allowing him to approach in his own time will help him continue to gain confidence.Crispin will be best suited to adopters who understand the needs of scared ex-breeding dogs and who will give him all the time he needs to settle at his own pace. He would be happy to share his home with another kind and confident resident dog in his new home. However, in the right home, with owners who are around enough to reassure him and who have experience with ex-breeding dogs, he could also be the only dog in the home.One thing Crispin has discovered is just how much he loves going for walks! He gets wonderfully excited when it's time to head out, twirling around and eagerly waiting by the front door. Once out, he walks beautifully on a lead, is very sociable with other dogs he meets, enjoys exploring new places, and travels well in the car. Walking has become one of his favourite activities and is a lovely way to watch his confidence shine through.As Crispin has now experienced life in a home, he has become familiar with many of the sights and sounds of everyday living. However, he hasn't quite mastered house training yet, so his adopters will need to continue helping him learn with patience, consistency, and plenty of encouragement.Crispin has also shown that he forms incredibly strong bonds with his favourite person. He loves to be close by and wants to be involved in everything they are doing. Because of this, he showed signs of separation anxiety in his previous home when left for more than a couple of hours. His ideal home would therefore be one where someone is around for most of the day, and where any time left alone can be built up very gradually, helping him feel safe and secure.Crispin has a cataract in his right eye and is developing a cataract in his left eye. He has had dental work and unfortunately did need to have all of his teeth removed, so he will need to stay on a soft diet for the rest of his life. He has Grade 2 patella luxation in both hind legs, although this may continue to improve with gentle exercise as he builds muscle.Crispin is a gentle soul who has had a difficult start in life, but he has already shown that, with kindness and patience, he is capable of making wonderful progress. He is looking for a very special person who will understand his worries, celebrate his achievements, and enjoy watching him continue to blossom into the loyal and loving companion we know he can be.Crispin has a travel document, which says he is 7 years old, but we do feel he could be a little older than this.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

name: Ursula
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can now walk on a lead and harness, but need more practice.

I am learning about house training in my foster home, but will need more training.

I have a bilateral Grade 2 patella luxation.

Ursula is a sweet little lady who has come into our care from a breeder and is now enjoying life in a foster home, where she has been starting to experience home life for the first time ever. She is still slowly coming out of her shell and can easily become overwhelmed by new situations, but overall she is a very gentle girl who is making steady progress. When she does become worried, she can panic and may choose to make the wrong decision purely out of fear. On occasion, she has nipped when frightened, so she will need understanding adopters who can recognise when she is feeling overwhelmed and give her the gentle support she needs.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home with adopters who have experience of scared ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace.

Ursula takes comfort from having a kind and confident dog around her and will need a resident dog in her new home who can help her understand that new things are not always scary. She would benefit greatly from having a canine companion to look to for reassurance as she continues to settle and build her confidence. With the right support, we are sure Ursula will continue to become more comfortable and show her lovely personality.

Ursula had never lived in a home before moving to her wonderful foster home, but she is already doing wonderfully with her house training in her foster home. She happily sleeps through the night without any accidents and is essentially house trained, which is fantastic progress. Her adopters will still need to be patient and understanding as she continues to learn about home life and build her confidence.

She has started learning to walk on a lead and harness and though she still needs more practice to build up her confidence, she is doing well.

Ursula was underweight when she arrived but is gradually gaining weight and becoming healthier and stronger. She is a gentle little girl who needs a calm and understanding home where she can continue to build her confidence at her own pace. She may still become overwhelmed from time to time, but she is learning that she is safe and that her people will be there to reassure her.

Ursula has bilateral Grade 2 luxating patellas, but with gentle exercise this is currently not causing her any problems. Her adopters will need to be aware that this is a pre-existing condition and a disclaimer will apply, meaning it would not be covered by insurance. She also arrived with an umbilical hernia, which has since been repaired during her spay.

Ursula is a sweet and gentle little girl who has already made some lovely progress during her time in foster. She will need a family who can offer her patience, kindness and plenty of reassurance as she continues to find her confidence. With a kind resident dog by her side and a calm, loving home, we are sure Ursula will blossom into a wonderful companion.

Ursula has been given the Gift of Life by Anne Breen

Ursula has now had an amazing groom and looks like the poodle she is. So far Ursula has had no interest at all and I don’t understand why.

This baby is only 3 but has already seen things she struggles to forget. She’s only now understanding that hands can mean treats or gentle strokes and are nothing to worry about.

She’s now out walking with her doggy friends and loves all those smells. She is still nervous when someone approaches but I’m sure that will slowly pass once she realises they only want to say hello.

Ursula does easily panic and when this happens she doesn’t always make the right decision but with a calm voice and gentle hands she calms down.

She so deserves a calm and gentle household and relies on my resident dogs. So will require a friendly resident dog in her forever home.

Ursula has now been in foster for just over a fortnight and is still slowly coming out of her shell. She’s a very gentle girl but can easily get overwhelmed. When this happens she does tend to make the wrong decisions, but calms down fairly quickly.

She is gradually increasing her weight as she was underweight when she arrived.

Ursula will need a kind and gentle resident dog to help her understand new things are not always bad. Ursula happily sleeps through the night without any accidents and basically house trained. She has been diagnosed with grade 2 luxating patellas but with gentle exercise it’s not causing her any problems. She will have a disclaimer for this problem.

Ursula is a sweet little lady who has come into our care from a breeder. She is confident enough to come over and greet you when you approach, but she can lose confidence when it comes to being handled and may retreat until she feels safe again. With patience and gentle reassurance, she is continuing to grow in confidence every day.Ursula could be the only dog in a home, provided her adopters have plenty of time to help build her confidence and support her as she settles into family life. She could also happily live with a kind and confident resident dog who she can look to for reassurance as she learns about home life and continues to gain confidence.Having never lived in a home before, Ursula will need patient and understanding adopters to help her with house training and lead walking and all the new experiences that come with family life.Ursula is a gentle, affectionate little lady who simply needs a family willing to give her the time she deserves. With kindness, patience, and understanding, she is sure to blossom into a wonderful companion.Ursula has arrived with a bilateral Grade 2 patella luxation that may improve with gentle exercise but will need to be monitored in the home. Her adopters will need to be aware of this as it may not be covered by insurance. She has also arrived with an umbilical hernia that has been repaired during her spay.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Benji
description:
I could live with older, dog-savvy teens who respect my space.

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I'd like a secure garden to have fun playtimes in.

I walk on a lead and would enjoy a nice walk once a day.

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been neutered and am ready to find my forever home.

03-11-26 Benji is a beautiful, playful boy who originally came into our care as an unclaimed dog in 2024. He was adopted but has sadly returned to us because of illness in the family, meaning his owners were no longer able to care for him.

Benji is feeling a little out of sorts being back in kennels but is coping well. He is a super-loving boy who absolutely adores attention, cuddles and bum scratches. He has been spending lots of time in the office with us while his exercise is restricted and is always happy to soak up some fuss. He has lots of character and a wonderfully silly personality, and we know he would love nothing more than to be back in a home where he can relax on the sofa and enjoy life with his favourite people!

Benji can be a little reactive towards other dogs when out on walks, but having spent time in a home, he has made some lovely improvements. He is currently kennelled with a friend and we feel he could potentially live with another suitable dog or as an only dog. His adopters will need to be understanding of his needs and willing to continue supporting him with his training around other dogs. When Benji was initially with us, he could snap at feet when leaving his kennel, but this behaviour has improved massively since his time in a home. He is generally much better around doorways, although he can still become uncomfortable if someone lingers in a doorway or enters without greeting him, so his adopters will need to be mindful of this.

Having lived in a home before, Benji is familiar with the sights and sounds of everyday life and will hopefully settle back into a home routine with a little time. He needs a calm home with adopters who understand his breed and can give him the consistency and reassurance he needs. He can live with teenagers aged 16 and over who understand his needs and will respect his space.

Benji was castrated and had nasal wedge surgery in 2024. His exercise and activity levels are currently being managed, so he will need adopters who are happy to accommodate his reduced exercise needs. However, he will need to be monitored for any future treatment he may need.

Benji really is a lovely little man who is full of character and has so much love to give. He is a typical silly Frenchie who is desperate to get back to being the couch potato he deserves to be! With a calm home, understanding adopters and plenty of cuddles, we know he will be so happy to have a sofa to call his own again.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Sunny
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog my size or larger to help me settle in & I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have an undershot jaw & I have had 4 of my teeth removed during spay!

27-08-26 Sunny is a sweet girl who has come to us from a breeder and is trying her hardest to be brave. She was very briefly adopted, but after a few days in her new home it was clear that her and the resident dog weren't a good match and so she has returned to our care.

Sunny loves other dogs and still looks to her kennel friends for comfort and reassurance, so she will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to and lean on as she continues to grow in confidence. She will be best suited to a home where any resident dogs were her size or larger and were fairly confident and well socialised. We think she will settle quickly in the right home, and with patience and encouragement, we’re sure her lovely personality will really begin to shine.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace.She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who are kind and sensible and will give her the time she needs to settle in.She will now happily approach you for a fuss and is easy to handle, which is lovely to see as she begins to settle in and discover the world around her. Sunny arrived with us very matted, but she was such a good girl during her grooming session and took everything in her stride.

Sunny has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be kind and patient as she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She has started to learn all about walking on a lead and harness and though this is still new to her, she is doing well. Sunny is an amazing lady who has so much to look forward to and will make a wonderful addition to a loving and accepting home.

Sunny has arrived with an undershot jaw that does not seem to bother her, but will need to be monitored in her new home. She has had 4 teeth removed at the time of her spay.

Sunny has been given the Gift of Life by Victoria Charlton

Sunny has been on my section for more or less the whole time she’s been at the rescue, and I know we’re not supposed to have favourites, but I just love her so much! She’s SO comical and has such an infectious energy. She can make me laugh and smile by doing absolutely nothing. I can’t explain it, she’s just funny!

She absolutely loves toys and lights up every morning when I bring them to her kennel. She checks on every one and then will pick her favourite one and carry it into bed with her. So sweet! She also loves being in bed. Especially when she’s snuggled up with one of her kennel friends. Her favourite thing in the whole world though, is definitely food. She is such a greedy little monster when it comes to treat time or breakfast or dinner time. She will do pretty much anything if she knows she’ll get a yummy snack out of it. I’ve recently started harness training with her and this has been a huge help. I always have liver paste on hand and she’s doing so well with it. We’re still only walking around quiet places of the rescue currently, so she’s definitely not a pro yet, but she’s getting there!

If you have a house full of toys, love and cosy beds, please consider welcoming this cheeky little darling.

Sunny is a sweet girl who has come to us from a breeder and is trying her hardest to be brave. She was very briefly adopted, but after a few days in her new home it was clear that her and the resident dog weren't a good match and so she has returned to our care.

She will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who are kind and sensible and will give her the time she needs to settle in. She will now happily approach you for a fuss and is easy to handle, which is lovely to see as she begins to settle in and discover the world around her. Sunny arrived with us very matted, but she was such a good girl during her grooming session and took everything in her stride.
