name: River
description:
I need an experienced, adult only home with no visiting children.

I would prefer to be an only dog, but I have lived with another dog. See more below.

I would like a secure garden in a quiet area.

I can walk well on a lead and would like an active home.

I need experienced adopters to work on my reactivity with me.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

River originally came into our care in 2020 from a breeder and was adopted into a loving home. Sadly, her family later found they were unable to continue meeting her needs, and River has now returned to us.

River is a highly intelligent, affectionate girl who forms very strong bonds with her people. According to her previous home, once she feels safe she is extremely loving, enjoys close contact and seeks reassurance from those she trusts. She loves cuddles, gentle scratches, and being near her humans, and is very in tune with their emotions, often offering comfort when someone is feeling down.

River is a clever and enthusiastic learner who already knows a wide range of cues and enjoys training, enrichment and mental stimulation. She loves her toys, especially balls and tug toys, enjoys scent games such as “find it”, and is very food-motivated, peanut butter is her absolute favourite! She settles well at home, enjoys routine and structure, and is clean and non-destructive.

River enjoys her walks and would suit an active home with access to quieter walking routes. She walks nicely on a halti and enjoys being out and about, but can find busy environments overwhelming and may be reactive to dogs, vans or motorbikes when anxious. She will need confident handling and continued training, and should remain on lead unless in a secure area.

Although affectionate and loving, River is a sensitive dog and can struggle with unfamiliar people, visitors and loud or sudden noises such as fireworks. When frightened she may bark or retreat. For this reason, River is looking for acalm, quiet, adult-only homewithvery few visitors, ideally in arural or semi-rural setting. Her adopters must beexperienced with reactive dogs, patient, and willing to work at her pace while respecting her boundaries.

We are advised that River can occasionally display guarding behaviours towards her trusted humans, such as growling if another person enters the room while she is settled. This will need calm, confident and experienced management.

River is currently looking for a home as anonly dog, although she has previously lived with another small dog and may be able to live with a calm companion following careful introductions.

River may not be suited to everyone, but for the right home she will be an incredibly loyal, affectionate and rewarding companion who has so much love to give.

A bit about River from her previous home:

Riverwill need more than one meet and greet with her prospective adopters to allow her time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

I’m a staff member who hasn’t really worked directly with River. But we have a mutual understanding that I’m a friendly person who’s got treats… that’s about as far as my friendship with River has gone, until now.

However, I’d say she’s warming to the idea of me being a good friend. I get a bum wiggle and tail wag when she sees me now, and I get a paw in exchange for some tasty treats… a few fewer grumbles over the last few weeks.

Recently, I also had time to take River for a walk, an honour, as she’s very stranger-danger and has only a handful of staff members that she is a big baby around.

Now, the weather wasn’t great for said walk, and she definitely used her body weight to get more treats out of me. I happily obliged, as by the end of our short walk, River nuzzled me! She sat beside me looking for a head scratch and even sat in front of me, keeping a lookout while we waited for her kennel mum to come and get her.

You may think, ‘Why is the staff member so happy?’

Because River is a dog with boundaries and is not the typical dog that you see in a café or busy environment, just enjoying the scenery. She is reluctant to socialise with new people and prefers to keep her circle small and her environment on the quiet side. So, to even be willing to go for a walk with a staff member that she doesn’t socialise with often is a huge achievement for River.

If I had the right lifestyle for her, I’d 100% have her living the antisocial life with me, but I have hope that River is just waiting for the right home to see and appreciate her and all the quirks that just make her the most amazing dog you ever get to meet.

River is honestly the sweetest girl once she knows and trusts you.

Recently, I’ve been taking River around our reception area and spending some quiet time with her, helping her learn that people she doesn’t know don’t have to be scary.

River is now happily taking treats from numerous members of staff she doesn’t know, something that might seem so small to some, but for River and everyone who knows her it’s a massive achievement!!

Once River lets you into her world and that special bond is built, she will be your best friend for life. She has so much love to give; she just needs someone willing to take the time to earn it!

I really, really hope River’s people find her soon. It’s heart breaking to see such a loving girl waiting in kennels when I know just how much happiness she could bring to someone’s life.

River may need a little time to trust you, but i can promise you, she will be worth every second.

River and I have a complicated relationship. I have worked with river more or less since she came in to us. She seemed to have forgotten this fact and decided I was no longer a trusted person. To combat this, I decided to work closely with her to see if I could change her mind.One thing I learnt about river early on is that she loves a walk! So, naturally, I put her harness and muzzle on and took her for a 30 minute walk. She enjoyed this very much so! The next day, I took her out on a longer walk, around an hour. River will not get tired. She is happy to walk for days and happier still if you take her for so long. On one of our walks, we stopped by a church, had some cuddles and did some tricks. She’s very clever.

Another activity I did with her was taking her to our big sand yard (a large enclosed field), letting her roam free and playing fetch. Great for exercise, mental stimulation and, in turn, trust building. She loves to fetch, definitely one way to get a higher standing in her good books.As well as this, I spend a lot of time with her in her kennel, just trying to show her I’m a trustworthy human.

In conclusion, we now have a much better relationship. It goes to show; things that seem small actually make a big difference. River is an extremely clever, beautiful girl. She does not warm to everyone but, with time, patience and perseverance to break through to her, she will be your best friend. Ideally, she requires a home with no other dogs, a human who can spend the majority of their time with her, take her out and give her the stimulation she needs.

Just wanted to share quick update for our wonderful River! Her kennel mum has been working on showing River that visiting the vets isn’t always a scary ordeal. Today, I popped in with her to see how it was going. I was SO impressed!

Although she was hesitant to come in, once in the vets she settled enough to have the biggest cuddles (River gives the BEST cuddles). We spent 5 minutes or so telling her how beautiful and amazing she is and made sure to head out before she got too worried.

River is honestly one of those special, once in a lifetime dogs. Once she bonds with you, she has this incredible ability to make you feel like the most important person in the world. She gives you her whole heart. Whoever adopts her will be so lucky to have her in their life!

Our gorgeous girl River is still on the search for a new home and family and hopefully her forever one. River is continuing to do very well here at the rescue and has progressed so much since being back with us.

Having lived in a home River knows a lot of commands and has been very well taught. She's clean in her kennel and isn't destructive at all. Although, she has lived in a home before she does still struggle at times with busy environments and people she doesn't know. When shes greeted by someone she doesn't know she will bark out of uncertainty but if you offer her a treat she tends to make friends with you pretty quickly. There were only a couple of people who could work with River initially when she came back to us due to her being so overwhelmed and worried but now half the rescue can work with her so shes made massive progress and I couldn't be any prouder of her.

She walks lovely on the lead and absolute loves going out for walks or down the big yard where she also loves to play fetch. We have been training River to understand that going to the vets isn't all that scary. We have been desensitising her by walking her up the vet steps and just sitting there for a moment praising her. Before, she wouldn't even go up the steps so for her to do this and sit there for a moment is massive for her. Our next step will be to open the vets door and go from there. River is such a special girl and when she trusts you she loves you with her whole heart and she genuinely does make you feel so loved. Being Rivers Kennel Mum is honestly the best and having all that love and affection from her is just utterly amazing.

River is continuing to do incredibly well here and is trusting more and more people she meets each day. It’s been lovely to see her confidence grow as she builds good relationships with other people. As part of her ongoing desensitisation, we’ve been walking River around the front of the rescue and gradually up towards the vets. This helps her learn that these environments are safe and nothing to worry about. Throughout this training we give her plenty of praise and tasty treats, and she is responding really well.

Considering everything she’s working through, she’s doing brilliantly. River is muzzle and Halti trained, as she can be reactive to certain dogs and can be strong when she first heads out on walks. We are working on her reactivity daily, and she is improving.

Her future adopters will need to continue with this training to help her keep progressing and feeling secure. River is an absolute darling. She has such a loving nature and truly makes you feel so loved when you spend time with her. With the right support and understanding, she would make a wonderful companion and a very special addition to the right home

River is a gentle girl who has previously lived in a home and is already kennel clean, giving her a great foundation for her next chapter. She can be a little cautious with new people at first, but with time and patience, she soon shows her sweet, affectionate side. Once she trusts you, River forms a lovely bond and just wants to be close to her people. She’s looking for a kind, understanding home that will give her the reassurance and love she deserves.

Quiver, Trevor, Clever Trevor, Trev, Piggy, Pig, Squirrel, Egg Nog Dog

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Pushkin
description:
I need a calm and quiet home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have met cats fine.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on harness but I can be spooked. Let's take it slow!

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home. Read below for more information!

Pushkin has come to us from a breeder and is still waiting for her loving forever home. She can be nervous when meeting new people and experiencing unfamiliar situations, but her confidence has grown so much during her time with us. She simply needs a little time to warm up and figure people out, and once she feels comfortable, her wonderful personality really starts to shine through.

Pushkin is a truly special girl with a fun, quirky nature and an incredibly affectionate side. She has become a firm favourite with the staff who know her, and once you have built a bond with her, it is something really special. She gets so excited to see her favourite people, especially first thing in the morning, and is always ready to put a smile on your face. She loves being around people she knows and, once comfortable, wants to be by your side all the time. She is a very affectionate girl who will happily jump up for attention whenever you sit down! She is also very easy to handle and pick up when needed.

Pushkin takes a great deal of comfort from the company of other dogs and becomes worried and stressed when left on her own. Because of this, she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help guide her through life. She gets along beautifully with other dogs and has happily shared kennels with several different companions. She is wonderfully respectful around food and is happy to eat alongside other dogs without bothering their bowls. She also has no issues sharing toys, bedding or treats. She really is a lovely, easygoing canine friend.

Pushkin has made lovely progress with her walking and is now comfortably walking on just a lead. However, with new people, we would still recommend using a harness until she has had time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them. Some things can still make her nervous when out and about, so her adopters will need to be patient and reassuring, helping her feel safe as she encounters new experiences. She gains confidence from having another dog alongside her and would benefit from a calm canine friend to help her navigate the world.

Pushkin has never experienced life in a home before, so her new family will need to be kind, patient and understanding as she learns all about home life. She will need help with house training and learning the everyday routines that most pet dogs take for granted. She enjoys treats, so positive reinforcement will be a wonderful way to help her learn and build confidence. She will need a home with adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. We would consider homing her with dog-savvy teenagers aged 13+. She will also need a secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft to ensure her safety while she adjusts to her new home.

Pushkin has met cats around the rescue well and could possibly be homed with a dog-savvy cat. She has also been treated for an ear infection.

We honestly cannot understand why this wonderful girl has not found her forever home yet. She has so much love, fun and affection to offer, and once she trusts you, she will become a very special part of your life. With the support of a canine friend, patient adopters and a home where she can feel safe, Pushkin will make an incredible addition to the family. Please give this lovely girl the chance she deserves; we know she has so much happiness, laughter and love to bring to her forever home.

Pushkin has been given the Gift of Life by Cherry Lewis

I am beyond baffled as to why my special girl hasn't found her forever home yet. She is such an incredible girl.

Once you have a bond with her it doesn't go away, and we have such an incredible bond and we're both very excited to see each other first thing in the morning, she always puts a big smile on my face.

Pushkin is now comfortably walking on just a lead but with new people I would still suggest using a harness until she is comfortable with you.

Pushkin is so good with other dogs, she has been in kennels with a few different dogs since being here and has always been fantastic, I can feed her with other dogs and she is so good, very respectful and doesn't go sticking her head into their bowl while they're still eating, also toys, nice bedding, treats, etc never an issue with sharing.

She is such an affectionate girl once she is comfortable with you, and just wants to be around you all the time, I honestly can't sit down when around her without her excitedly jumping on me, but I wouldn't change it, she's just amazing.

Pushkin is also very easy to handle and pick up if needed.

I honestly don't know what more I can say to convince people to adopt her, she would be an incredible addition to your family, and will fill your days with so much love, joy, happiness and laughs, please give her a chance.

The last two weeks or so Pushkin, along with her kennel buddy Maggie, has been joining the big play group down the big play yard everyday (weather permitted) and she absolutely loves it. She enjoys saying hello to the other doggies there and play chases with some of them, it's so cute to watch, it makes my heart melt. It's amazing to see how much her confidence has grown, she really is blossoming.

She is quite attached to me, and does get excited to see me, she loves getting fusses from me, and is never too far from where I am if we're in a yard together, so if you like having a little extra shadow following you around she could be the girl for you.I took her out today on just a lead instead of a harness and she did amazingly, that being said for safety reasons and until she is comfortable and feels safe with you adopters would need to walk her on a harness for a while.Pushkin is just an amazing girl, I can't praise her enough and I'm always more than happy to talk about her with anyone who is interested in adopting her.

This beautiful lady brightens up my days, and as this has been a difficult week for me personally, she has been there to put a smile on my face through it.She can be nervous when you meet her initially but her confidence has grown so much she just needs time to warm up to you and figure you out, but once she's comfortable and her personality comes out she's just so much fun, and so loving. She has such a quirky personality and I absolutely adore her.Pushkin does walk on a harness, although some things do make her nervous still when out on a walk so adopters will need to be aware of this and let her know she is safe as well as some encouragement.Pushkin gets along with pretty much all dogs, any dog she has been kennelled with or introduced to for a play date she has always been so good, is fine with toys around and also eats well around the other dogs.She has never lived in a home before so her new family will have to show her the ropes and help her with her house training, be encouraging and use positive reinforcement, she does enjoy treats so they should be a big help.I'm not lying when I say I genuinely get excited to see her everyday I'm at work, she really is a little ray of sunshine.

Pushkin has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for a loving forever home. She is initially quite nervous and unsure, but once you spend some time with her she starts to come out of her shell and even begins to enjoy a fuss.

Pushkin is a sweet girl who simply needs understanding and the chance to build her confidence at her own pace. She will be looking for a calm and quiet home where she can settle in gradually and continue to blossom. She takes a great deal of comfort from the company of other dogs and becomes quite worried and stressed when left on her own. Because of this, she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and show her that the world isn't such a frightening place.

Pushkin has never experienced life in a home before, so her new family will need to be kind, patient and understanding as she learns all about home life and new skills such as house training. She has made lovely progress with her harness training and is now walking on a harness, although she is still a little nervous when out and about. She is much more confident when she has another dog alongside her, so having a calm canine companion to help reassure her on walks will be a real benefit. She will need a home with adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She will also need a secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft to ensure her safety while she adjusts to her new home.

With plenty of love, reassurance and the support of a canine friend, Pushkin will continue to grow in confidence and become a wonderful companion. She is a lovely girl with so much potential, and we can't wait to see her enjoying the happy life she truly deserves.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Jinx
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I will need a secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I have a sore eye that is being monitored.

Jinx is an exceptionally frightened boy who has come into our care from a breeder. He will do all he can to run away and hide from us, and it is heartbreaking to witness just how scared he is. However, after just over a month in our care, his personality is slowly beginning to shine through. Although he remains very wary and unsure, he is starting to make lovely little steps forward. He now gets excited when he sees a familiar face, happily wagging his tail and sniffing a hand, even if he isn't quite ready for anyone to come too close. These may seem like small steps, but for Jinx they are huge achievements, and it is wonderful to see his confidence growing.

Jinx has also begun harness training and is taking to it really well! He is now venturing down to our big play yard, where his playful puppy side is starting to emerge. It is lovely to see him becoming a little more curious about the world around him as he gradually learns that he is safe.

Jinx will need a kind and confident resident dog in his new home, as this will be a much-needed support system to help him settle and gain confidence. We have not yet cat tested him, but given what we have seen so far, we feel it is unlikely that he would be suitable to share a home with cats.

As Jinx has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. His harness training is progressing well, but his adopters will need to continue this gently and at his own pace. He will need a quiet, experienced home with people who understand ex-breeding dogs and appreciate that building trust with him will take considerable time, patience and kindness.

Due to his nervous nature, Jinx is currently a flight risk and will need a very secure garden with boundaries of at least 6ft. He may also need to be muzzled for formal handling, such as veterinary visits, to help keep everyone safe and make these experiences as comfortable as possible for him.

Jinx arrived with a sore eye, so we are continuing to clean it and make sure he is comfortable while we assess this further.

Jinx still has a long way to go, but he is making progress every day, and it is lovely to see his gentle, playful personality beginning to emerge. He needs a very special home filled with patience and love, where his adopters understand that trust will take time and are happy to celebrate every little achievement along the way. With the support of a kind canine companion and people who will let him move at his own pace, we hope Jinx will continue to blossom and discover the safe and loving life he deserves.

Jinx has been given the Gift of Life by Lesley Beattie

Jinx has now been with us just over a month, and although Jinx is still a very scared boy, his personality is slowly starting to shine through. Jinx has now begun harness training and is taking to it really well! He even now adventures down to our big play yard where his puppy side is really starting to show!  Jinx also now gets really excited to see me, he doesn’t allow me very close but he will happily wag his tail, and sniff my hand!

This might sound like the smallest thing, but for myself and Jinx this is a massive win! Every day is confidence is showing more and more.

Jinx just needs a home with loads of patience and love, and people who will understand trust is going to a long time.I can’t wait to see Jinx blossom more and more each day.

Jinx is an exceptionally frightened boy who has come into our care from a breeder.He will do all he can to run away and hide from us, and it is heartbreaking to witness just how scared he is. Despite his trust issues, he has allowed a small amount of fuss, although he remains very wary and unsure of our intentions. He will need lots of time, patience and gentle handling while he learns that he is safe.Because of this, Jinx will need another kind and confident dog in his new home, and this dog will be a much-needed support system for him as he begins to settle and gain some confidence.We have not yet cat tested Jinx, but given what we have seen from him so far, it is unlikely that he would be suitable to share a home with cats.As Jinx has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. He will need a quiet, experienced home with adopters who understand ex-breeding dogs and are prepared to be very patient with him.Due to his nervous nature, Jinx is currently a flight risk and will need a very secure garden with boundaries of at least 6ft. He is a very scared boy and may need to be muzzled for formal handling eg. vet visits.Jinx has arrived with a sore eye, so we are keeping on top of cleaning it and making sure he is comfortable while we assess this further.Jinx has a long way to go, but the fact that he has already allowed a little fuss shows that there is a gentle side beneath all those worries. We hope that with the right canine companion, experienced adopters and lots of patience, he will slowly learn to trust and discover the safe and loving life he deserves.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Margate
description:
I need an experienced adult only home with no visiting children.

I would prefer to be an only dog, though may be able to live with a calm female.

I’m active and would love a large, secure garden to let off steam.

I have lots of energy and need an active home that loves adventures.

I can resource guard and will need adopters who can manage this.

I’m fully vaccinated and neutered. I have received treatment for an ear infection.

Margate has now spent over2 and a half years in kennels. That’sover 900 daysof waiting. Waiting while thousands of people have walked past his kennel. Waiting while his friends have come and gone. Waiting for someone to truly see him.

Everyone here adores Margate - he’s smart, affectionate, and bursting with personality. But love from staff isn’t the same as a forever home, and Margate is more than ready for his next chapter.

Since staying with us, Margate has received a dental treatment and had a cyst removed from his back left leg.

Margate came to us from a breeder in November 2023. He'sincredibly intelligent,loves a challenge, and will do absolutely anything for a tasty treat. He picks up tricks like lightning - he knows “sit”, “paw” and “speak” and he’s always ready to learn more. He thrives when his brain is engaged and would be an excellent candidate for scent work or activities like cani-cross (on-lead only!). He’s been described asone of the smartest dogs we’ve ever worked with.

He'svocal, a bit cheeky, and loves to tell us when it’s breakfast time - you can hear his excited barks all the way from the car park. He may come off as bouncy and bold, but beneath the surface, Margate is a sensitive soul who, sadly, has beenlet down by humans before. He can get worried easily, especially in overwhelming environments like the vet, where he becomes a bit of a puddle of anxiety (though he's muzzle-trained and manages with support).

Margate does require avery specific kind of home, and we won’t sugar-coat it - he’s not a “starter dog.” He needs:

Margate ispossessive around food, toys, and bedding, likely stemming from insecurity in his past. These behaviours are manageable - we’ll give guidance - but his adopters will need tounderstand and work with him, never punish or push him beyond his limits. Setting him up for success is the key.

Margate will test you - not because he's difficult, but because he's clever, spirited, and sensitive. But once you have his trust, you’ll havea bond that’s unbreakable.

Because Margate isn’t a dog you can bring home on a whim. He’s forsomeone extraordinary. Someone who sees past the behaviours and looks into his big, soulful eyes and says,“I’ve got you now.”

Margate has come so far during his time with us - he’s learned manners, made friends, gained confidence, and shown us theincredible potentialhe holds. But he deserves so much more than life in a kennel, no matter how much we love him.

Margate isnot for everyone, but if he’s for you - truly for you - then you are in for the mostrewarding journey. He’ll love you with his whole heart, and you’ll wonder how you ever lived without him.

If you think you could behis person, please don’t wait another day.

Margate’s forever is long overdue. Let’s not make him wait another year.

Margate will need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

“My boy, Margate… I see all of you, and I’ll love you like you’re my own until your forever person comes along. I’ll be so jealous of whoever gets to share their life with you.”

Mr Margate (AKA Best Boy, the love of my life, Margherita Pizza, Maggie Moo, Margaret, and many other ridiculous nicknames) is approaching his third year here, and we're not letting a single day of his stay be wasted.

His days are full of so much love. So many people are part of Margate's family, and he adores seeing them all when he walks around the rescue or goes up to reception. He gets treats, but he's become quite fussy, so he'll only accept the best of the best.

He loves his long walks, his regular Margate-approved volunteers, his big yard time, sniffing as many sniffs as he can, and occasionally, he loves rolling in poo, which I am not so pleased about, but the boy enjoys it, so I don't judge.

He is the most super special boy who has so many adoring fans, and I am the founder of that fan club. I know his right home is out there; he just needs to wait a bit longer. But every single day here matters, and we're showing him all of the love, understanding, and support that we could possibly offer.

Mr Margate has utterly blown me away in recent times.Around a month ago, Margate had an unfortunate accident in the play yard, which lead to an emergency vet visit and his front paw needing stitches.

As one of the kennel managers, I see and interact with Margate regularly, but unfortunately I don’t get the luxury of working closely with him. But I think the story below highlights how much this beautiful boy wants to do the right thing.

I was the first person to get to Margate after his accident, do you know what he did when I got to the yard? He limped over to me, sat at my feet and cried out. I know some will say it’s anthropomorphism, but I am so sure in that moment, he was asking for help!

We had to carry Margate up to the top of the rescue to clean him off and assess his wounds, Margate is muzzle trained which meant we could safely assess his wounds without any risk - but honestly, he was SO well behaved. Yes he needed reassurance that he was, in-fact, being a good boy, but he blew me away with the trust he gave us.

We cleaned him up and quickly realised he needed to go for assessment with an out-of-hours vet. So, phone calls were made, and off he went, carried into a strange car and taken to a strange place and sedated for stitches… where again, he was such a good boy despite the pain he must have felt.

Upon return, poor Margate was on strict rest, with only short toilet walks, having bandage changes every few days, boots on and off for walks… his whole routine was turned upside down. Living in kennels, his world is already quite small, and these changes, although temporary and for his own good, made his world even smaller.

This is where Margate began to struggle a little; in pain and insecure, some of his guarding behaviours (which we haven’t seen for a long time) did resurface. Luckily, Margates main carer knows him inside & out, like the back of her hand, and created a plan for everyone to follow to help build his confidence back up. Just some small adjustments to keep him & everyone around him safe, which worked beautifully and we got to see the best of our boy again, despite still being on rest.

A few weeks have now passed, Margate has had his stitches out, his wound has healed beautifully - and he fully back to being our incredible, charismatic, clever, fun loving boy! It’s the highlight of my day to see Margate, he is so happy meeting everyone.

All of this is to say, Margate may not always be an “easy” dog, but he SO wants to do the right thing. Occasionally, his worries overwhelm him, but for someone with experience and patience, the love and joy you will receive in return will be so worth it.

Margate is, hand on heart, one of the most phenomenal dogs I’ve ever met, and after nearly nine years at Many Tears, I’ve met a lot of dogs! He is going to be someone’s absolute best friend and the most wonderful adventure companion.

His profile already covers all of his basic needs, so I won’t repeat those here, but I can honestly say that not a single day he’s spent in kennels has been wasted.

He has grown, learned, and loved so much during his time with us. His confidence has blossomed, he absolutely adores people, and he has made some lovely doggy playmates. He knows exactly which treats are his favourites, and he’s settled beautifully into his routine. He heads out to his yard at 9am, then off to reception to spend time with more people (and, of course, collect more treats!).

Throughout the day, different staff members make time to visit him for extra cuddles and attention, and he often spends my entire lunch break relaxing in the yard on sunny days. This is something he enjoys every second of.

Margate is such a genuinely lovely guy, which makes it all the more surprising that he’s had to wait so long. He has the sweetest nature and seems to want nothing more than to be everyone’s best friend. While he’s here, he’s made some great female play friends and absolutely loves spending time with them every day, soaking up the companionship and fun.

In one month's time Margate will have been waiting a full two years for his forever family to find him. He's been in our care for a full 23 months, that's around 700 days, he's never been adopted or gone to foster so he's not been returned to us, he just has been in the rescue for all that time, waiting.

The first picture is his original booking in photo, a very worried boy who arrived knowing nothing about what we would do for him and how much love he'd come to find in this place that should be a pit stop until their forever home is found. But he slowly grew to love people, he started to let his true personality shine through and he started to learn how to be the goodest boy in so many ways. We flash forward to today and I can still see his insecurities at times, these may never truly go away, but we help him through it all and he is one of the best dogs I have ever known.

I love him as I love my own adopted dogs and I try to let him have as much time and love as I can give him to help him not feel like a single day in kennels is wasted. Because this is two years of his life that he won't get back, so I damn well hope that I, and everyone else who has had a part in his journey, makes every single moment count!I know he'll always have his quirks and he does need a specific type of home with people who understand and can positively manage his guarding behaviours so that he doesn't feel the need to show these often. But he's such a good boy, he's so loved by all of us at the rescue, he's so smart and beautiful and funny and loving and such good company. I love every speckle of white he's grown on his face in these two years, I love every snuggle we have and every single moment he looks to me to let me know that everything is going to be okay.He needs the right home but more importantly, he deserves the right home, the right people. If I could move heaven and earth to give him his perfect life, I would.I do want him to leave the rescue, but only to people that can fully commit to keeping him safe and listening to every single guideline and boundary that we give them. One of which is that HE MUST be kept on a lead at all times when out of fully secure areas, his prey drive is very high and he deserves to be given everything he needs to be kept safe from being harmed, which means keeping him on a lead!I shall continue to love him with every day that he's in my care, as well as every day after he finds his perfect home and I wave him off.I'll be so happy that he was chosen but he's going to leave a huge hole in my heart. He's truly one in a billion.If you feel you may be the right fit, please read his profile completely and fill in a very detailed application form. We will be very particular about where he goes, because that is the least he deserves from us.My handsomest boy, Mr Margate

It's strange really, the bond you have with a dog on your section, especially if they're a long stayer.

They aren't your dog and yet you love them as though they are, you cuddle them and tell them how amazing they are, you pour your heart and soul in to them and try your very hardest to make each and every day special in some way because their time in kennels shouldn't be a waste or simply a means to an end.. it should matter and they should be living their life whilst waiting for a family of their own.

This is hard to do when there are so many dogs to care for, but you try to do the best for them and to make sure they know how truly special they are.

This is very much the case for my best friend, Margate (AKA Maggie, Margaret, Marjorie, Marge and he responds to all these names). He is the epitome of special, he does need a specific home with people who don't put him in bad situations, but when the right people come along, they'll be adopting a dog that will give them an absolutely smashing best mate and although I am desperate for his forever home to find him, the thought of saying goodbye to the most special boy with a heart the size of the moon and a brain that's double that still. I will feel as though I'm missing a huge chunk of my heart.

That's the job though, and in a strange way, that sadness is the most rewarding part. To be a part of finding them the perfect match that will not love them in spite of their quirks, but because of them. Someone who will choose them day in, day out with a certainty that just grows with every passing day. The love a dog shares with you, no matter for how brief or long, as many will know, stays in your heart forever.

I shall miss my best mate, Margate. His family will love him the longest, but I loved him first and I am so so grateful for that.

If you are interested in being the exceptionally lucky human that shares their life with this beautiful soul, then please read his profile and apply if you feel that you can give him all he needs.

Another day for Margate in kennels, after another week, another month... I'm just hoping that he doesn't have to wait until the another year mark.

Margate has been waiting for seventeen months for his ideal home to find him, that's 506 days in the same place, with people who adore him, but they're not just his people. He has to share his time with so many other dogs that are waiting for their forever homes, but none have been waiting as long as him.

He does require a special home, with people who can help him thrive and who will not fail him! But as long as they understand his needs and set him up for success, they'll get so much in return.

Margate needs a cat, child (resident and visiting) and small furry free home. He needs mental stimulation and he needs a good deal of exercise too, he is smart, so so soooo smart and this is where his humans will have to try and be smarter.

Margate learns everything very quickly and will need to have clear, set boundaries in his new home from the get-go. He will need to be given his own bed, that he learns is his bed and that he isn't allowed on the sofas or other furniture, especially to begin with. He will need a home that understands how to enrich his life, to use his brain and that LOVES a good walk. He could walk for miles. He could potentially do cani-cross as he loves to run, but Margate needs to be kept safe at all times, so he will need to be kept on a lead in anything he does (unless in a secure rented dog field area). He has a high prey drive and a nose that rivals the very best sniffer dog. If you had treats in your pocket at some point this year, he'll know.

The best set up for Margate would be a home that could adapt a room to be his area that is free of food and where he could go to sleep at night, if visitors came round or if you had to pop out to go shopping etc. He needs this to be his area that helps him feel safe and secure.

Although he can act like a big tough guy, underneath it all he is extremely sensitive and can get very worried by things.

How can we blame him for being this way? He's been let down by humans over and over again, he has had thousands of people walk by his kennel during his stay and no one chooses him.. I know that in a home that FULLY understands him and puts everything in place to set him up to succeed, then he will be the bestest boy you could ever wish to know. His heart is the size of the whole universe and he just needs someone to see him and commit to him, then they'll see what I see too. My boy, Margate, I see all of you and I'll love you like you're my own until your forever person comes along. I'll be so jealous of the person who gets to share their life with you.

Disclaimer - although he picks up agility things quite quickly, this is not something he should do to a competitive level as the environment of the events would not benefit him.

It is now over a year since Margate joined us here in Many Tears.  That’s 365 days of seeing the same kennel, and the same routine and watching his friends leave whilst he gets left behind. This year it’ll be the second Christmas in kennels and whilst others are snuggled up in a warm home and spoilt with presents, it’ll be another day in kennels for him.  Everyone here at the rescue loves Margate!

What can I say that already hasn’t been said about this wonderful boy ??

He’s a real character, smart and witty. Every morning I hear him from the staff car park and you know that he’s announcing breakfast time for the whole rescue!  At times he can be loud and bouncy but deep down he’s just a little baby who loves a good snuggle.

Margate really has improved over the year, learnt new tricks, muzzle trained, met loads of new friends and loves meeting new people! He’ll happily walk past volunteers and once instructed to sit and wait he will receive a fuss.

So far Margate has only needed the muzzle for the vets as a precaution, but he tends to turn into a puddle of mush as he’s actually quite scared of the vets.

Margate does have issues regarding high value treats, toys and beds. This is resolved by removing any food in the area, removing any toys from the yard before play time and using multiple blankets for bedding. This is something that can be discussed and helped with for potential adopters.

All Margate needs is for adopters to understand his requirement’s and who are willing to work with him in a home environment.  He is such a beautiful wonderful boy who really is wasted here in kennels?

Margate is still absolutely thriving and learning every day. He is such a clever boy who enjoys his training and the company of his kennel friend. He has come such a long way, but in a home he could truly excel as long as his new humans know how to keep his training progressing and his mind busy. I really hope he breaks free soon.

Margate is one of those dogs that once you know him, you fall head over heels in love with him. He is one of the smartest dogs I've ever worked with, picks things up incredibly quickly and tries very hard to please you. He would be the perfect only dog for someone who wants to pour lots of time in to training to build a strong bond with him and who will understand that he will train you if given a chance. He's a super special guy with so much love to give, he just needs the right person to choose him and fully commit.

Margate is a super cool bocker. He loves long walks and his time in the yard. He thrives with anything to get his brain working, so stimulation games are an excellent way of working Margate. The best way to work with him is definitely food, he will do anything for a tasty treat. Be careful though as Margate can be food possessive. As you can see by the pictures he is such an affectionate boy who loves a good fuss, to go with that he is just absolutely handsome! Margate has been in kennels for some time now and he does cope well with being in kennels, but he would just absolutely thrive in an active home with someone who is willing to keep him busy and stimulated. While he's been with us he's always had a female kennel friend but he would also be an excellent only dog, so you have the best of both worlds with Margate, but due to his exuberant nature he might grate on any resident dogs a bit . Margate is a stunning young man with bags of personality and he loves all the attention and will need an experienced owner as he is a rambunctious soul. Margate is an absolute star and deserves the best life possible, if you feel you can offer him his best life get in contact. Be sure to read all the previous updates on Margate also to get the best overall idea of this smart little man. This wonderful boy has been in kennels for far too long now and is ready to find his forever home and new loving family. Will you give him the chance to progress to the next chapter in his life?

Margate is a unique boy. Firstly, Margate will need an owner with some experience under their belt, to make sure his rehabilitation is successful. It is probably best that he is homed as an only dog, as Margate struggles to get along with some dogs due to his boisterous personality, which can be overwhelming. This doesn't mean he can't be homed with another dog, as he has had a few kennel friends at the rescue that he gets along great with, he just prefers human attention. Margate will not trust strangers 100% straight off the bat , he's always excited to see people and interact with them, but to build a bond of trust takes some time. However this is an experience that I've found extremely rewarding. I discovered this when I took him to the vets for an intimate checkup, and was surprised to discover that he would only allow me to carry out the checks. It absolutely melted my heart to know that he had complete faith in me. He really is a sweet, colourful personality with so much love and energy to give, he just needs some time, love and repetition with a regular owner to steer all that energy in a positive direction

Since his last update Margate has been enjoying learning tricks and enjoying fun little games. We have learnt to "sit" "paw" and to" speak". Margate enjoys his treats so was very keen to learn and being as smart as he is, picks up training in a flash. He is a very vocal boy and will bark until I give a treat. I do not give in and he will stop and wait patiently. Margate does need to learn manners so will need adopters to remind him of this and to show Margate right and wrong.

Margate has come on so well since being here and I must admit that I do have a soft spot for him. He enjoys his walks but does pull a little when he has found a sniff, but can easily be managed with lead training. I'm currently teaching Margate to sit when I stop walking, to get his pulling under control, and as Margate is food motivated, it’s easy to see that this can be managed with little trouble. He is already  getting the hang of it!

Margate does jump up on you and can jump quite high, so adopters will need to encourage Margate not to jump up, which I am currently showing him, but again he is a very smart boy who is eager to learn. He is a funny, friendly, and vocal boy who will needs adopters to be mindful of his needs and issues and redirect him properly for him to be the best boy he can. He is still kenneled with his friend who both still continue to share their bed and space together with no problems. He is still only young and I can't wait to see him flourish more than what kennel life can offer him. Please read Margate's profile and updates and see what an amazing boy he is. He is perfect for someone that loves to share an active lifestyle with their dog, and we can’t wait to see pictures of him on all his future adventures!

Margate is a gorgeous boy who I have spent a lot of time getting to know recently and has come along way since his last update. He greets you with a waggy tail and excitement when he knows you and does enjoy a gentle fuss. He is also getting used to his name and when you call him he will turn to you. Margate has very high energy and needs an active household who enjoys long walks and adventures and are able to stimulate him mentally as well as physically. He also walks on a lead but can pull, this can easily be managed with lead training and I believe will settle once he gets to go on regular adventures with his new family as he enjoys the sniffs of the world . Margate loves to learn and play and due to his breed, he will need adopters to understand the Bocker breed and the energy they have. Margate currently is kennelled with a female cocker and they spend their time together playing in the yard and rolling around in their beds together. They both get on very well!

Due to Margate's resource guarding, him and his kennel friend have bedding and blankets rather than plastic normal beds and they both share this with no problems. Margate does have food guarding issues  and is fed separately from his kennel friend. This can also be managed in a home with another dog if he is separated at feeding times. Margate does take treats from you when his kennel friend is present and has not shown any issues towards them but this still needs to be remembered. I have been visiting him when I'm not on the same section to issue treats around other dogs in proximity to get him used to being in the same space around other dogs with food and treats. With these small issues, Margate will need an adult home with no children.

Margate has mastered a few tricks with treats, learning to sit and give paw. He gets very excited when you ask him but need to tell him firmly. Margate can be jumpy and will jump on you so he will need a firm voice to encourage him manners. Margate learns quickly so I think teaching him house training, lead training as well as other tricks and manners will come quickly for him, especially with treats!

He is a stunning boy and overlooked here at the rescue. If you have a Bocker sized hole in your heart and are active, love long walks, adventures and fun. Please consider applying for Margate.

Hi! My name is Margate I am 2 years old male Bocker (Cocker X Beagle) and have found myself at this amazing place called Many Tears. When I first arrived, I was extremely worried with my new surroundings, and adapting back to kennel life was very tough. I have spent a little time in a home but because of my high energy levels and need for adventures my family wasn’t able to provide this so unfortunately through no fault of my own I have set out on an adventure to find my new forever home. In my new home I would need a child free home with no visiting children. In my new home I will need someone who understands my breed and have had experience with similar breeds. I am currently in a bedroom (Kennel) with a female Bocker called Nova. We don’t interact too much but we do enjoy one another’s company so I could be happy having another friend in my new home upon having a meet and greet at the rescue. I can also be an only dog as long as I have a loving owner who plays lots of games with me. I have mastered walking on a lead and I absolutely love to explore and go on walks so having a busy home who is as on the go as I am would really benefit my energy levels. I still struggle a little to find the toilet but if I’m shown I will definitely find a way to go in the right place. when I meet new people I can become a little shy and anxious so go slow with me, have a kind voice and I will wag my tail and ask you for some fuss. After spending a day with you i trust very easily and I will become your best friend. If you’d like to meet me I am currently at the many tears rescue.Margate is still waiting for his forever home at Many Tears and despite his struggles around food and resource guarding from humans and dogs when food is involved, all he needs is an experienced home with the ability to adapt and help Margate with this. He will bring so much joy into your home and he can't wait to be a cherished member of the family where he can go on lots of adventures and finally be loved.

Margate is a stunning but very confused boy who is overwhelmed to be here and has been through so much change recently. He has come to us from a breeder to find his forever home. Initially when you first meet him he is mistrustful of strangers and unsure about being handled - he will make his worries known by growling. However once you have spent a few minutes in his company showing that you are safe he quickly warms up to you and jumps all over you for love and attention. We suspect he may have lived in a home before and then returned to the breeder hence his being unsure of people initially which is fair enough, poor boy! Margate already walks on a lead and would probably prefer to be an only dog.  Margate will need a cat free home as he is far too interested in them and a home without children or visiting children as he would find them too much. Margate may need help learning to live in a home and being taught housetraining skills. Margate is such a poor soul who just wants to be loved and to feel safe. Margate would need a home that is experienced in resource guarding and can help Margate work through his struggles. Margate can resource guard when he has food or high value treats/chews/bones around both dogs and people so this would need to be managed with an environment set up to ensure lovely Margate is set up for success.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Paris
description:
I'd like a quiet, experienced, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I haven't tried walks yet, a secure garden will be fine for now.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

30-09-26 Paris is a scared girly who is not used to being handled. She has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start and is not a fan of human touch at the moment.

When we have needed to get close to Paris for health checks, we have had to carefully corner her so that we can pick her up. She panics and shakes, but she does allow us to handle her and, once she is safely in our arms, she eventually cuddles into us and allows us to carry out her checks. This shows us that although she is very frightened, she is beginning to understand that we are not going to hurt her.

Paris will need another kind and confident dog in her new home, and this dog will be a much-needed support system for her as she settles in and starts to find her confidence.

As Paris has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training, lead training and the other basics of home life. She will need an ex-breeding experienced, adult-only home with adopters who understand just how much patience and reassurance she will need.

Paris is a very worried little girl right now, but once she is given the security of being held, we can see that there is a much softer side to her. We hope that with time, patience and the support of a reassuring canine companion, she will slowly learn to trust and enjoy the happy new start she deserves.

Paris has been given the Gift of Life by Margaret Hunter

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Irene
description:
I can live with older, dog savvy teenagers, aged 16+ who respect my space.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I am new to lead walking, and would like to continue this once I have settled in.

I have lived in a home before so know the basics.

I have Grade 3 bilateral luxating patellas.

21-10-26 Irene is a nervous little lady who has come to us from a breeder. Although she is still unsure, she shows lovely glimpses of wanting to be confident. If you are patient with her and crouch down to her level, she'll quietly come over to give you little kisses, showing just how much love she has to give once she feels safe.

Irene will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home that she can lean on as she learns about trust and settles into home life. She has recently moved to a foster home where she is learning all about the routines of home life. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who are sensible and will allow her time to settle in. She will need a home that has experience with ex-breeders that can provide her with the assurance she deserves.

Irene is new to lead walking but has enjoyed plenty of walks with her foster mummy and is gaining her confidence on the lead. She will need a home without cats as she has met cats while out and about and was a little too interested in them. Irene is a truly lovely girl who just needs time, patience and plenty of TLC. With an understanding home and a canine friend by her side, we're sure she will continue to grow in confidence and become a wonderful companion.

Irene has been assessed by our vets who have noted that she has Grade 3 bilateral luxating patellas. These aren't causing her any issues at the moment and may improve with gentle exercise as she builds muscle. They will need to be monitored by her adopters and their vet and her adopters should be aware that any future treatment relating to her luxating patellas will not be covered by insurance.

Irene has been given the Gift of Life by Trudie Williams

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Moxy
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult-only home.

I will need a kind, calm resident dog to show me the ropes. I'm unsure of cats.

I would like an extra-secure garden to spend time in.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I am currently in a foster home where I am learning about home life!

Moxy is a worried little girl who has come to us from a breeder and is now in foster, where she is beginning to show her lovely, affectionate personality. She can be unsure around new people, but as she learns to trust you, more of her sweet nature shines through. In the evenings, she will come to her fosterers for a cuddle on her own terms, which is lovely to see as she continues to grow in confidence.

Moxy will need an adult-only home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand that she needs time, patience and kindness to settle into her new life. A calm, quiet environment with minimal disruption will be important, as will having a gentle, quiet resident dog to help her feel safe and guide her through home life. Moxy has struggled with a more vocal dog in her foster home, so her canine companion will need to be calm and considerate of her needs.

Moxy has never lived in a home before and is learning about house training and everyday routines in foster. Her new family will need to continue this patiently and gently introduce her to lead walking. She has shown signs of digging, so she will also need an extra-secure garden to keep her safe.

Moxy arrived with sore eyes, and our vet noted that her lower eyelid is irregular, although this is not currently causing her any issues. We are also concerned that her vision is significantly reduced, as her depth perception seems affected. She may bump into things or be startled when other dogs approach unexpectedly, so her adopters will need to understand her visual difficulties and help her navigate her surroundings safely. She also arrived with sore skin and old concrete sores, which we hope will continue to improve.

Moxy has already made lovely progress and is gradually learning to trust the people around her. She will need a special family who can offer a peaceful home, a calm canine companion and the understanding she needs to feel secure. With time, patience and gentle reassurance, we hope this affectionate little girl will continue to blossom and discover just how lovely life can be.

Moxy has been on our section for a few weeks now & she is such a delight to be around.

Dependent on where Moxy is will decide which side of Moxy you will get. Both sides are a truly beautiful dog, but one is incredibly sad & shut down and the other is a wonderful, affectionate girl who truly tries her hardest to be brave.

When in the kennel you’ll find Moxy in the back, she’ll appear sad, broken & totally overwhelmed. She tries to dig a lot, and burrow herself behind any beds she can find. We have swapped these beds out with a big comfy duvet now where she likes to chill in the corner. However I do think she sees it as her safe space, where she will hide from the outside world. Once she’s out of that kennel, and running to the yard she will wag her body in its entirety as she greets other kennels desperately trying to make new friends.

Even in the yard, Moxy can still feel overwhelmed and will sit in the corner & dig at times, and we’ve even tried taking her out on a harness but she remains frozen. But once she’s comfortable in the company she is around, she is the most affectionate girl. She happily sits next to you, gives you kisses and that tail really does not stop wagging. Her company is joyous, and being one of her trusted people is so incredibly rewarding, and brightens every day I spend with her.

Moxy’s people will need to take it easy with her, need to understand exbreeders, and be patient & kind along her journey at home. Mixing her nervous character along with her poor eyesight, being at home is likely to be very scary for her. As one of her kennel mummies, I can vouch for her & tell you that gaining her trust, and gaining her as a family member will be the most fulfilling experience, and one I am extremely jealous of. Moxy deserves love, care & a place to feel safe after all this time feeling scared & overwhelmed.

Moxy, like a lot of ex breeder dogs, is a very nervous dog. When I first met her, she wouldn’t leave the back, didn’t want me to get near her and I had to carry her back and forth from the yard. On my second day with Moxy, she ran straight to the yard as I opened her kennel door and, once I entered the yard, she was jumping all over me, kissing me, genuinely thrilled to see me. This is behaviour that truly shocked me in the best possible way.

It’s now been a couple of weeks since I first worked with her and the affection she shows me and the confidence she found has only grown. She’s truly incredible.Around new people, she reverts back to shutting down and hiding in the back. Despite this, we still have an incredible relationship. Moxy needs to be shown she can trust you.

Once this girl trusts you, you’ll see the same side I see. You won’t see this side if you met her on a show around of our kennels or even if you were let in her kennel to socialise her. This is something you can only experience from adopting her and progressing her like we do. I truly love her with all my heart. Take a chance on her and I have no doubts you’ll experience the same as I.

Moxy is a very worried little girl who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is feeling quite overwhelmed to find herself here at the moment and is in need of lots of TLC, patience and reassurance. Once she gets to know you, she does start to come out of her shell and then enjoys a gentle fuss.

Moxy will need a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need plenty of time to settle in at her own pace. She will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help her learn how wonderful her life can be now. We would consider homing her with old, dog savvy teenagers.

Moxy has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her. Her new family will need to be kind and understanding as she learns all about home life, including new skills like house training and walking on a lead. She will need gentle encouragement and understanding as she settles in.

Moxy is a very sweet girl who has had a difficult start in life. She now needs someone who will give her the time, patience and love she needs to blossom. With a kind canine friend by her side and a quiet, understanding home, we hope she will slowly gain confidence and discover how lovely life can be.

Moxy has arrived with slightly sore eyes and our vet has noted her low eyelid is irregular but doesn't feel this is causing her any issues at the moment, but will need to be monitored moving forwards. Although she can see, her vision isn't the best, but she doesn't let this slow her down and gets around well. She also arrived with sore skin and old concrete sores, which will hopefully feel much better soon.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Maggie
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I can be an only dog or live with one dog my size or larger. I cannot live with cats!

I'd like a secure garden to play in that has 6ft fencing.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been spayed and have had 4 teeth extracted.

Maggie spent the first few years of her life at a breeders & originally came to us when she was 5 years old. She was adopted in January 2025 & spent 16 months in a home. She ended up back in our care & has since waited to find her forever. Maggie really is just the sweetest, most special girl. Whilst she is shy at first, she bonds incredibly closely with her people. She has a cheeky, playful side & loves to fling herself around with a tennis ball. She bounces & prances around the yard just keeping herself entertained. Maggie is our girl who helps the scared dogs be brave. Maggie shows them how it’s done & truly she has been the helping hand for so many dogs since she has been with us. She has seen kennel friends come & go, yet she still waits in kennels. Maggie is a happy dog even in kennels, especially when she is with any of her favourite people. She is so affectionate & truly a little shadow. You gain a best friend when you’re loved by Maggie. Our groomer has said multiple times that she is an absolute delight to groom. Maggie loves nothing more than to roll around in mud, sand, leaves, she gets mucky quickly. Her & our groomer are well acquainted now so she is well adjusted to grooming.

Sadly, Maggie was returned to us following an incident involving one of the smaller resident dogs in her previous home. While out in the garden one evening, Maggie became frightened by the other dog barking, and although we don't know exactly what happened, the interaction unfortunately ended in a fight. They struggled to make up or comfortably co-exist afterwards, so Maggie will need a carefully chosen home where everyone can feel safe and settled.

Maggie is looking for a calm and quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and can give her plenty of time, patience and understanding to settle at her own pace. She can be worried by men and initially barked at the male resident in her previous home, although with time, patience and gentle handling, she slowly began to come around. We are continuing to help her build positive relationships with men here, and she has bonded well with a male staff member who is part of her care team.

Maggie is very people-oriented and, once she knows and trusts you, she becomes an incredibly loving and devoted companion. She is particularly attached to her main carer and loves following her around, enjoying fuss and cuddles. When she first returned to us, she was very shy and unsure of new people, but she has since settled in wonderfully and has made lovely progress.

Although Maggie previously lived with another dog, her home will need careful consideration following her return. We would now consider her as an only dog in the right circumstances, with experienced adopters who have plenty of time to help her settle. Alternatively, she could live with a calm, confident resident dog of a similar size or larger. She has shared her kennel with several different dogs since returning and has been wonderful with them, happily sharing food and toys. She also enjoys play dates with a larger group of dogs in our big play yard. I cannot live with cats, so I will need a home without small furries.

Maggie is very food-motivated and loves her treats, which will be helpful when settling into her new home. She can already walk nicely on a lead and harness without pulling and will often check back with you for reassurance. Having previously lived in a home, she will be familiar with home life, although she may need some reminders of her house training.

On one occasion in her previous home, Maggie became tangled in her harness and panicked, biting the hand of the male owner who was trying to help free her. This was an isolated incident caused by fear, but it is important that her new family understands how she may react when frightened or overwhelmed. She will need calm, gentle handling and people who can recognise when she is worried and give her the reassurance and space she needs.

Maggie has also shown that when she feels stressed or overwhelmed, she may try to escape by climbing. For this reason, she will need a very secure garden with boundaries of at least 6ft to help keep her safe.

Maggie has had four teeth extracted, and this should be kept in mind as part of her veterinary history.

Maggie has so much love to give to the people she trusts. In the right calm and understanding home, with experienced, patient and dog-savvy adopters who allow her to settle at her own pace, we are confident she will continue to flourish and become a truly wonderful companion.

Maggie has yet again made some new canine friends here at the rescue, Jinx - Hound and Hayley - Poodle and yet again she has been amazing with them, showing them that us staff here at the rescue are nothing to be feared and helping them understand that a human touch can be loving and kind, she has been incredible with a lot of our scardies and the change you then see in those dogs, a lot of it thanks to Maggie, is amazing, she really is a special girl.I also had to bath her (again) this past week as due to her fur type and the weather she gets dirty rather easily, but, she is so good in the bath, she's very tolerant of the water and being shampooed. When it comes to brushing and drying, she is also easy, for the most part she either just stands or lays there which makes her quicker to dry.She really is a dream dog and she's still waiting for her forever home after almost 5 months. Winter is coming, that means cold days and nights, and although we do everything we can here at the rescue to ensure that they're all comfy and warm, it's nothing compared to the home comforts of being wrapped up in her own blanket, snuggled up with her own family knowing, who wouldn't want that for her?Please consider Maggie, she's one of our most overlooked angels and it genuinely makes me sad that no one seems to take an interest in her. I promise you she'll make an amazing companion and a true best friend just like she is for me while I'm her kennel mum.

Maggie aka Magaluf, Magarita, Mags or Miss Maggie is a special girl. She's the kind of dog that once she's comfortable with you, you instantly feel the love she has for you from her and it's such a lovely feeling, she is very affectionate and loves her people more than anything, well, maybe not more than her food or treats but we're her second favourite.

Maggie's confidence has grown so much these past months that she's even helped some of our more shyer residents come out of their shells, and by them seeing how she is with us makes them realise that they too can be like that with us and have fusses and cuddles etc.

She is an incredible girl and it truly baffles me as to why she keeps getting overlooked. She is beautiful both inside and out and has such a fun personality. She is good with other dogs but won't necessarily need to be rehomed with another dog as we believe that she is confident enough to be an only.

Maggie will become a best friend and a true companion, and I know I'm probably a lot biased being one of her kennel mums but she truly is so so special and anyone would be lucky to have her in their life.

Maggie has settled into rescue life beautifully, but having spent over a year in a home, we are really desperate to get her back into one ASAP!

Since her arrival, Maggie has been kenneled with our lovely Bocker Eddie whom she gets along with wonderfully. She does enjoy her time with him, and would happily live alongside one resident dog - male or female, her size or larger!!

During Maggie’s time here she has formed a wonderful bond with her kennel mums who she absolutely dotes on. She’s even bonded with a kennel dad who has said she’s an absolute sweetheart, and he’s had no trouble with her too, which is so good to hear.

Maggie's kennel mummies describe her as loyal, affectionate, and loving. She really looks to them for reassurance, and when they’re around nothing else matters. Seeing as she’s grown so much in confidence, we’re happy to say she can now also be homed as an only dog too in the circumstance her adopters have lots of time to spend with her!!

Maggie isn’t really too fussed on playing with toys, but what she does love is her food & treats so gaining her trust will be a breeze!

A dog like Maggie is absolutely wasted in kennels, she’s already lived a life at home & we are so desperate to get her back into one!!

Maggie is a sweet Cockapoo who originally came to us from a breeder. She was adopted for around 16 months, but has sadly returned to us from a home following an incident with one of the smaller resident dogs in the home. During the evening, while out in the garden, Maggie was frightened by the other dog barking. Although we don't know exactly what happened, the interaction unfortunately ended in a fight and they struggled to make up or co-exist after this.

Maggie is a very shy and sensitive girl who is wary of strangers, although she does allow handling. She is trying very hard to be brave and is beginning to show small signs of progress, even getting close to taking treats from our hands, though she is not quite confident enough just yet.

Maggie is not yet confident enough to be an only dog, so we feel she would settle best in a home with one calm and confident resident dog of a similar size or larger, who can help her feel safe and reassured as she adjusts.

As Maggie has previously lived in a home, she will be familiar with the sights and sounds of a home environment. However, she may still need some support with house training as she settles into a new routine. Maggie can already walk on a lead, so she would enjoy one or two walks around the local area with the resident dog when she is settled in.

Maggie is particularly worried by men and did initially bark at the male resident in her previous home. With time, patience, and gentle handling, she slowly began to come around. Unfortunately, there was also an incident where Maggie became tangled in her harness and, in a panic, bit the hand of the male owner who was trying to help free her. Because of this, Maggie will need a calm adult-only home with patient and understanding adopters who have experience or understanding of the challenges that can come with rehoming ex-breeding dogs.

Since Maggie has been with us, she has shown that when she feels stressed or overwhelmed, she may try to find a way to escape by climbing. Because of this, she will need a very secure garden with boundaries of at least 6ft to help keep her safe and prevent any potential escape attempts.

Once Maggie knows and trusts someone, she is a very sweet and happy girl. In the right calm and understanding home, with patient and dog-savvy owners who are willing to let her settle at her own pace, we are confident she will continue to make wonderful progress and slowly come out of her shell.

Maggie is currently being treated for an ear infection in the left ear.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Flash
description:
I would like to be the only animal in my new home.

I would like a good sized, secure garden to explore.

I can walk on a lead but find this very overwhelming at the moment.

I have entropion in both eyes, which have been repaired by the vets.

Flash is a truly striking Standard Poodle with a big personality, a sensitive soul, and an oversized puppy spirit. He first came to us after his previous owners could no longer give him the time and exercise he needed.
